if \tau\leq 1 then the first statement of
(4.32) follows immediately from
the operator norm bound (4.27), which implies
|\frac{1}{n}\langle\operatorname{Tr}\mathbf{J}^{s+\tau,s}\rangle|\leq\|\mathbf{J}^{s+\tau,s}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq C . For \tau\geq 1 , we apply
a Bismut-Elworthy-Li representation for \nabla P_{t} :
For any f:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R} with uniformly bounded first and second derivatives,
\nabla P_{t}f(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{0})=\frac{1}{t\sqrt{2}}\left\langle f(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{t})\int_{0}^{t}(\mathbf{J}^{r,0})^{\top}\mathrm{d}\mathbf{b}^{r}\right\rangle
where \{\mathbf{b}^{t}\}_{t\geq 0} is the Brownian motion defining
\{\boldsymbol{\theta}^{t},\mathbf{J}^{t,0}\}_{t\geq 0} [31, Lemma 4.2].
Applying this with t=1 and f_{i}=P_{\tau-1}e_{i} , with the needed regularity of f_{i} ensured by [30, Proposition A.2(c)], we get
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf{e}_{i}^{\top}\nabla P_{\tau}e_{i}(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{0})=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf{e}_{i}^{\top}\nabla P_{1}f_{i}(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{0})=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,\frac{1}{n}\left\langle P_{\tau-1}\operatorname{id}(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{1})^{\top}\int_{0}^{1}(\mathbf{J}^{r,0})^{\top}\mathrm{d}\mathbf{b}^{r}\right\rangle.
Thus, noting that \langle\int_{0}^{1}(\mathbf{J}^{r,0})^{\top}\mathrm{d}\mathbf{b}^{r}\rangle=0 and
applying Cauchy-Schwarz, Jensen’s inequality, and the Itô isometry, we have
\displaystyle\sqrt{2}\left|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf{e}_{i}^{\top}\nabla P_{\tau}e_{i}(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{0})\right|
\displaystyle=\left|\frac{1}{n}\left\langle\Big(P_{\tau-1}\operatorname{id}(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{1})-\langle\boldsymbol{\theta}\rangle\Big)^{\top}\int_{0}^{1}(\mathbf{J}^{r,0})^{\top}\mathrm{d}\mathbf{b}^{r}\right\rangle\right|
\displaystyle\leq\left\langle\frac{1}{n}\|P_{\tau-1}\operatorname{id}(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{1})-\langle\boldsymbol{\theta}\rangle\|_{2}^{2}\right\rangle^{1/2}\cdot\left\langle\frac{1}{n}\left\|\int_{0}^{1}(\mathbf{J}^{r,0})^{\top}\mathrm{d}\mathbf{b}^{r}\right\|_{2}^{2}\right\rangle^{1/2}
\displaystyle\leq\left\langle\frac{1}{n}\|\boldsymbol{\theta}^{\tau}-\langle\boldsymbol{\theta}\rangle\|_{2}^{2}\right\rangle^{1/2}\cdot\left\langle\frac{1}{n}\int_{0}^{1}\|\mathbf{J}^{r,0}\|_{F}^{2}\mathrm{d}r\right\rangle^{1/2}
(4.33)
\displaystyle\leq C\left\langle\frac{1}{n}\|\boldsymbol{\theta}^{\tau}-\langle\boldsymbol{\theta}\rangle\|_{2}^{2}\right\rangle^{1/2},
the last inequality applying (4.27).
Applying this bound with \boldsymbol{\theta}^{s} in place of \boldsymbol{\theta}^{0} shows
\left|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf{e}_{i}^{\top}\nabla P_{\tau}e_{i}(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{s})\right|\leq C\,\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{1}{n}\|\boldsymbol{\theta}^{s+\tau}-\langle\boldsymbol{\theta}\rangle\|_{2}^{2}\,\bigg|\,\mathbf{X},\boldsymbol{\theta}^{s}\right]^{1/2}.
Then applying the coupling bound (4.22),
we obtain the first statement of
(4.32). The second statement of (4.32)
follows similarly, applying the above
bound (4.33)
with \tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0} in place of \boldsymbol{\theta}^{0} and using instead
the coupling (4.20).
Taking the n\to\infty limit in (4.30) and
(4.32), we have
(4.34)
|R_{\theta}(s+\tau,s)-r_{\theta}(\tau)|\leq Ce^{C\tau}\cdot e^{-cs},\qquad R_{\theta}(s+\tau,s)\leq Ce^{-c\tau},\qquad r_{\theta}(\tau)\leq Ce^{-c\tau}.
Then, choosing a small enough constant \iota>0 such that the first bound
satisfies
Ce^{C\tau}\cdot e^{-cs}\leq C^{\prime}e^{-c^{\prime}s} when
\tau\leq\iota s/(1-\iota) (i.e. s\geq(1-\iota)(s+\tau) ), we may write
\displaystyle\int_{0}^{t}|R_{\theta}(t,s)-r_{\theta}(t-s)|\mathrm{d}s
\displaystyle=\int_{(1-\iota)t}^{t}|R_{\theta}(t,s)-r_{\theta}(t-s)|\mathrm{d}s+\int_{0}^{(1-\iota)t}|R_{\theta}(t,s)-r_{\theta}(t-s)|\mathrm{d}s.
Applying the first bound of (4.34) for the first integral
and the latter two bounds of (4.34) for the second integral,
this shows
\int_{0}^{t}|R_{\theta}(t,s)-r_{\theta}(t-s)|\mathrm{d}s\leq Ce^{-ct}.
Applying the first bound of (4.34) when \tau\leq\iota s/(1-\iota) and the latter two bounds of (4.34)
when \tau\geq\iota s/(1-\iota) , we have also
|R_{\theta}(s+\tau,s)-r_{\theta}(\tau)|\leq C^{\prime}e^{-c^{\prime}s}.
This shows all statements of part (c).
Part (d). Let
L^{2}(\mu_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}) be the space of functions f:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R} for which
\langle f(\boldsymbol{\theta})^{2}\rangle<\infty . Since
\{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}} is reversible, for each fixed n , there is a
family \{E_{a}\}_{a\geq 0} of orthogonal projections onto increasing closed
linear subspaces of L^{2}(\mu_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}) (corresponding to the spectral
decomposition of the generator) such that for all f,g\in L^{2}(\mu_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}) and \tau\geq 0 ,
\langle f(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0})P_{\tau}g(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0})\rangle=\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-a\tau}\mathrm{d}\langle f(\boldsymbol{\theta})E_{a}g(\boldsymbol{\theta})\rangle
[4, Theorem A.4.2]. Applying this with the coordinate
functions f=g=e_{i} and averaging over i=1,\ldots,n , there is
then a positive measure \mu_{n} (depending on n and \mathbf{X} ) for which
(4.35)
\frac{1}{n}\langle{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}}^{0\top}P_{\tau}\operatorname{id}(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0})\rangle=\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-a\tau}\mu_{n}(\mathrm{d}a).
The bound (4.11) implies
\int_{0}^{\infty}\mu_{n}(\mathrm{d}a)=\frac{1}{n}\,\langle\|\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}\|_{2}^{2}\rangle\leq C . For any M,\tau>0 , we have also
\int_{0}^{M}\mu_{n}(\mathrm{d}a)+e^{-M\tau}\int_{M}^{\infty}\mu_{n}(\mathrm{d}a)\geq\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-a\tau}\mu_{n}(\mathrm{d}a)=\frac{1}{n}\langle{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}}^{0\top}P_{\tau}\operatorname{id}(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0})\rangle
so
(4.36)
\int_{M}^{\infty}\mu_{n}(\mathrm{d}a)\leq\frac{1}{1-e^{-M\tau}}\left(\frac{1}{n}\,\langle\|\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}\|_{2}^{2}\rangle-\frac{1}{n}\langle{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}}^{0\top}P_{\tau}\operatorname{id}(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0})\rangle\right).
By Itô’s lemma, Cauchy-Schwarz, and (4.11),
\displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\,\frac{1}{n}\langle\|\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}-\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}\|_{2}^{2}\rangle
\displaystyle=\frac{2}{n}\langle(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}-\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0})^{\top}[\mathbf{X}\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}-U^{\prime}(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t})]\rangle+2\leq C\left(\frac{1}{n}\langle\|\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}-\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}\|_{2}^{2}\rangle+1\right),
and hence Grönwall’s inequality shows
(4.37)
\frac{1}{n}\langle\|\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}-\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}\|_{2}^{2}\rangle\leq C(e^{Ct}-1).
Then by Jensen’s inequality, also
\frac{1}{n}\langle\|\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}-P_{t}\operatorname{id}(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0})\|_{2}^{2}\rangle\leq C(e^{Ct}-1) . Applying this to (4.36), for all n ,
\int_{M}^{\infty}\mu_{n}(\mathrm{d}a)\leq\frac{C^{\prime}(e^{C\tau}-1)^{1/2}}{1-e^{-M\tau}}.
Taking \tau=1/M and M\to\infty shows that the sequence of measures
\{\mu_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty} is uniformly tight, and hence converges weakly along a
subsequence of n to a positive finite measure \mu on [0,\infty) . Then
(4.18) and (4.35)
show that c_{\theta}(\tau) admits a representation
(4.38)
c_{\theta}(\tau)=\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-a|\tau|}\mu(\mathrm{d}a)\text{ for all }\tau\in\mathbb{R}.
From this representation and dominated convergence, we see that
c_{\theta}:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R} is continuous, and its restriction to (0,\infty) is
smooth where derivatives may be computed under the integral. Since
\mu is a positive measure, this implies also for all \tau>0 that
c_{\theta}(\tau)\geq 0,\qquad c_{\theta}^{\prime}(\tau)\leq 0,\qquad c_{\theta}^{\prime\prime}(\tau)\geq 0.
By the fluctuation-dissipation relation for the diffusion
\{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}} (c.f. [31, Lemma
4.1] applied with the coordinate functions A=B=e_{i} ),
for any \tau>0 we have
(4.39)
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\langle\mathbf{e}_{i}^{\top}\nabla P_{\tau}e_{i}(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0})\rangle={-}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\left[\frac{1}{n}\langle\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0\top}\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{\tau}\rangle\right].
As a function of \tau , the left side is uniformly equicontinuous
on any compact interval of [0,\infty) for all n , by the same argument as
above that established the equicontinuity of (4.26). Then
by Arzelà-Ascoli and the identities (4.18)
and (4.31), we have
r_{\theta}(\tau)=-c_{\theta}^{\prime}(\tau)\text{ for }\tau>0.
Thus for all \tau>0 ,
r_{\theta}(\tau)\geq 0 and r_{\theta}^{\prime}(\tau)={-}c_{\theta}^{\prime\prime}(\tau)\leq 0 .
Since the equicontinuity of the left side of (4.39)
includes \tau=0 , the identity
(4.31) implies that r_{\theta}:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R} is continuous at
0, so there exists a right derivative c_{\theta}^{\prime}(0^{+})={-}r_{\theta}(0) . Since
\nabla P_{\tau}e_{i}=\mathbf{e}_{i} at \tau=0 , (4.31) shows that
r_{\theta}(0)=1 , and hence c_{\theta}^{\prime}(0^{+})=-1 .
∎
We now turn to Lemma 4.2 on the analysis of R_{g},C_{g} .
Proof of Lemma 4.2.
We extend the definitions of R_{\theta},C_{\theta} to \mathbb{R}^{2} by setting
R_{\theta}(t,s)=0 for all t<0 or s\notin[0,t] , and
C_{\theta}(t,s)=0 for all s<0 or t<0 . We also extend r_{\theta},r_{\theta}^{\prime} to
\mathbb{R} by setting r_{\theta}(\tau)=0 for \tau<0
and r_{\theta}^{\prime}(\tau)=0 for \tau\leq 0 .
We will apply the following convolution bound: If
A_{1},\ldots,A_{p}:\mathbb{R}^{2}\to\mathbb{R}^{2} satisfy
|A_{k}(t,s)|\leq C_{0}e^{-c_{0}|t-s|} for each k=1,\ldots,p and all s,t\in\mathbb{R} ,
then
\int e^{(c_{0}/2)|t-s|}|A_{k}(t,s)|\mathrm{d}s\leq C_{0}\int e^{-(c_{0}/2)|t-s|}\mathrm{d}r=4C_{0}/c_{0},
and hence
\displaystyle\sup_{s,t}e^{(c_{0}/2)|t-s|}|A_{1}*\ldots*A_{p}(t,s)|
\displaystyle\leq\sup_{s,t}\int e^{(c_{0}/2)|t-r|}|A_{1}(t,r)|e^{(c_{0}/2)|r-s|}|A_{2}*\ldots*A_{p}(r,s)|\mathrm{d}r
\displaystyle\leq(4C_{0}/c_{0})\sup_{r,s}e^{(c_{0}/2)|r-s|}|A_{2}*\ldots*A_{p}(r,s)|
\displaystyle\leq\ldots\leq(4C_{0}/c_{0})^{p-1}\cdot C_{0}.
Thus for all s,t\in\mathbb{R} ,
(4.40)
|A_{1}*\ldots*A_{p}(t,s)|\leq\left(\frac{4C_{0}}{c_{0}}\right)^{p-1}C_{0}e^{-(c_{0}/2)|t-s|}.
We will apply also the basic identity, if a_{1},\ldots,a_{k}:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R} are
integrable, then
(4.41)
\int a_{1}*\ldots*a_{k}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau=\prod_{i=1}^{k}\int a_{i}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau.
Part (a): We have
r_{g}(\tau)=\sum_{p\geq 1}\kappa_{p+1}\,r_{\theta}^{*p}(\tau).
By the fluctuation-dissipation relation (4.4) of
Lemma 4.1,
\int r_{\theta}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau=\int_{0}^{\infty}r_{\theta}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau=c_{\theta}(0)-\lim_{\tau\to\infty}c_{\theta}(\tau)=v_{*}-q_{*}.
Then by (4.41), for each p\geq 1 ,
(4.42)
\int_{0}^{\infty}r_{\theta}^{*p}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau=\int r_{\theta}^{*p}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau=(v_{*}-q_{*})^{p}.
Lemma 4.1 implies 0\leq r_{\theta}(\tau)\leq r_{\theta}(0)=1 for all \tau\in\mathbb{R} . Then also for each p\geq 1 ,
(4.43)
0\leq r_{\theta}^{*p}(\tau)\leq\int r_{\theta}^{*(p-1)}(s)\mathrm{d}s=(v_{*}-q_{*})^{p-1}.
The condition (4.6) then implies that the above series defining
r_{g}(\tau) is absolutely and uniformly convergent over \tau\in[0,\infty) .
Since each summand is continuous in \tau , this shows r_{g}(\tau) is continuous
on [0,\infty) . The bound (4.7) follows from
(4.42) and (4.6),
\int_{0}^{\infty}|r_{g}(\tau)|\mathrm{d}\tau\leq\sum_{p\geq 1}|\kappa_{p+1}|\int_{0}^{\infty}r_{\theta}^{*p}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau<\alpha.
For any integrable a:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R} that is continuous and supported on
[0,\infty) and continuously-differentiable on (0,\infty) ,
we have [a*b]^{\prime}(\tau)=a(0)b(\tau)+[a^{\prime}*b](\tau) . Thus
the derivative of r_{g} exists on (0,\infty) and is given by
(4.44)
r_{g}^{\prime}(\tau)=\kappa_{2}r_{\theta}^{\prime}(\tau)+\sum_{p\geq 2}\kappa_{p+1}\Big(r_{\theta}^{*(p-1)}(\tau)+[r_{\theta}^{\prime}*r_{\theta}^{*(p-1)}](\tau)\Big)
provided that this series converges absolutely and uniformly over
compact subsets of (0,\infty) . Note that by Lemma 4.1,
\int r_{\theta}^{\prime}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau=\int_{0}^{\infty}r_{\theta}^{\prime}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau={-}r_{\theta}(0)=-1.
Then since r_{\theta}^{\prime}(\tau)\leq 0 and r_{\theta}(\tau)\geq 0 ,
for any p\geq 1 , (4.41) implies
\displaystyle 0\leq{-}[r_{\theta}^{\prime}*r_{\theta}^{*p}](\tau)\leq-\int r_{\theta}^{\prime}*r_{\theta}^{*(p-1)}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau=(v_{*}-q_{*})^{p-1}.
Then (4.44) is absolutely
and uniformly convergent on (0,\infty) as claimed.
Each summand is continuous in \tau , implying
that r_{g}^{\prime} is continuous. Furthermore, from the
signs of r_{\theta} and r_{\theta}^{\prime} and the above calculations, we have
\int_{0}^{\infty}|r_{g}^{\prime}(\tau)|\,\mathrm{d}\tau\leq\kappa_{2}+\sum_{p\geq 2}|\kappa_{p+1}|\left(\int_{0}^{\infty}r_{\theta}^{*(p-1)}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau-\int_{0}^{\infty}r_{\theta}^{\prime}*r_{\theta}^{*(p-1)}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau\right)<\infty.
To establish exponential decay of r_{g}(\tau) , note that the convergence
condition of (4.6) implies
\limsup_{p\to\infty}|\kappa_{p+1}|^{1/p}(v_{*}-q_{*}+\varepsilon)\leq 1 .
Thus, for some p_{0}>0 , we have
(4.45)
|\kappa_{p+1}|\leq\left(\frac{1}{v_{*}-q_{*}+\varepsilon/2}\right)^{p}\text{ for all }p\geq p_{0}.
Then, letting \delta>0 be a small enough constant to be determined,
the bound (4.43) implies
\sum_{p\geq\max(\delta\tau,p_{0})}|\kappa_{p+1}|\cdot r_{\theta}^{*p}(\tau)\leq\sum_{p\geq\delta\tau}\left(\frac{1}{v_{*}-q_{*}+\varepsilon/2}\right)^{p}\cdot(v_{*}-q_{*})^{p-1}\leq Ce^{-c\delta\tau}
for some constants C,c>0 depending on v_{*},q_{*},\varepsilon . For
p<\max(\delta\tau,p_{0}) , we have by Lemma 4.1 and
(4.40) applied to A_{k}(t,s)=r_{\theta}(t-s)
that r_{\theta}^{*p}(\tau)\leq C^{p}e^{-c\tau}
for some C,c>0 , any p\geq 1 , and all \tau\geq 0 .
We also have |\kappa_{p}|\leq C^{p} for a constant C>0 and all
p\geq 1 , by Proposition A.1. Thus
\displaystyle\sum_{p=1}^{\max(\delta\tau,p_{0})}|\kappa_{p+1}|\cdot r_{\theta}^{*p}(\tau)\leq\sum_{p=1}^{\max(\delta\tau,p_{0})}C^{p+1}\cdot C^{p}e^{-c\tau}
\displaystyle\leq C^{\prime}e^{-c\tau}\cdot e^{C^{\prime}\max(\delta\tau,p_{0})}
for some constants C^{\prime},c>0 not depending on \delta . Choosing \delta
small enough ensures this is at most C^{\prime\prime}e^{-(c/2)\tau} for all \tau\geq 0
and a constant C^{\prime\prime}>0 (depending on p_{0} , in the case \delta\tau<p_{0} ). Combining the above two statements, for some C,c>0 ,
(4.46)
|r_{g}(\tau)|\leq\sum_{p\geq 1}|\kappa_{p+1}|\cdot r_{\theta}^{*p}(\tau)\leq Ce^{-c\tau}.
To bound R_{g}(t,s) , recall that
R_{g}(t,s)=\sum_{p\geq 1}\kappa_{p+1}R_{\theta}^{*p}(t,s) where
R_{\theta}^{*p}(t,s)=\int_{s}^{t}\mathrm{d}t_{1}\int_{s}^{t_{1}}\mathrm{d}t_{2}\ldots\int_{s}^{t_{p-2}}\mathrm{d}t_{p-1}R_{\theta}(t,t_{1})R_{\theta}(t_{1},t_{2})\ldots R_{\theta}(t_{p-1},s).
We establish analogues of (4.42) and
(4.43) for R_{\theta} :
Letting \varepsilon>0 be the constant in (4.6), Lemma
4.1 ensures there exists s_{0}>0 such that if t\geq s_{0} , then \int_{0}^{t}|R_{\theta}(t,s)-r_{\theta}(t-s)|\mathrm{d}s<\varepsilon/4 .
Hence
\int_{0}^{t}|R_{\theta}(t,s)|\mathrm{d}s\leq v_{*}-q_{*}+\varepsilon/4\text{ for }t\geq s_{0}.
Then
\displaystyle\int_{0}^{t}|R_{\theta}^{*p}(t,s)|\mathrm{d}s
\displaystyle\leq\int_{0}^{t}\mathrm{d}t_{1}\ldots\int_{0}^{t_{p-2}}\mathrm{d}t_{p-1}\int_{0}^{t_{p-1}}\mathrm{d}s\,|R_{\theta}(t,t_{1})|\ldots|R_{\theta}(t_{p-1},s)|
\displaystyle\leq\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\int_{s_{0}}^{t}\mathrm{d}t_{1}\ldots\int_{s_{0}}^{t_{k-1}}\mathrm{d}t_{k}\int_{0}^{s_{0}}\mathrm{d}t_{k+1}\ldots\int_{0}^{t_{p-1}}\mathrm{d}t_{p}\,|R_{\theta}(t,t_{1})|\ldots|R_{\theta}(t_{p-1},t_{p})|,
where we set t_{p}=s and
stratify the domain of integration t\geq t_{1}\geq\ldots\geq t_{p}\geq 0 by
the largest index k for which t_{k}>s_{0} , with k=0 if t_{1}\leq s_{0} .
Bounding |R_{\theta}(t_{j},t_{j+1})|\leq C for all j\geq k , this gives
\displaystyle\int_{0}^{t}|R_{\theta}^{*p}(t,s)|\mathrm{d}s
\displaystyle\leq\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\int_{s_{0}}^{t}\mathrm{d}t_{1}\ldots\int_{s_{0}}^{t_{k-1}}\mathrm{d}t_{k}\,|R_{\theta}(t,t_{1})|\ldots|R_{\theta}(t_{k-1},t_{k})|\cdot\frac{(Cs_{0})^{p-k}}{(p-k)!}
\displaystyle\leq\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(v_{*}-q_{*}+\varepsilon/4)^{k}\cdot\frac{(Cs_{0})^{p-k}}{(p-k)!}
(4.47)
\displaystyle=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{[Cs_{0}/(v_{*}-q_{*}+\varepsilon/4)]^{p-k}}{(p-k)!}(v_{*}-q_{*}+\varepsilon/4)^{p}\leq C^{\prime}(v_{*}-q_{*}+\varepsilon/4)^{p}
for a constant C^{\prime}>0 depending on v_{*},q_{*},\varepsilon,s_{0} , which is an analogue of
(4.42).
Similarly, first bounding |R_{\theta}(t_{p-1},s)|\leq C and applying the same
argument, we have
(4.48)
|R_{\theta}^{*p}(t,s)|\leq C^{\prime\prime}(v_{*}-q_{*}+\varepsilon/4)^{p-1}
which is an analogue of (4.43).
Choosing a small enough constant \delta>0 , and
applying (4.48) for p\geq\max(\delta(t-s),p_{0})
and (4.40) for p<\max(\delta(t-s),p_{0}) ,
the same argument as for r_{g}(\tau) above shows
(4.49)
|R_{g}(t,s)|\leq Ce^{-c(t-s)}.
To bound |R_{g}(t,s)-r_{g}(t-s)| , again fix a constant \delta>0 small
enough. Observe that (4.43) and (4.48) imply
\sum_{p\geq\max(\delta s,p_{0})}|\kappa_{p+1}|\cdot|R^{*p}_{\theta}(t,s)-r_{\theta}(t-s)^{*p}|\leq Ce^{-c\delta s}.
For the summands p<\max(\delta s,p_{0}) , identify r_{\theta}(t,s)\equiv r_{\theta}(t-s) and write
\displaystyle R_{\theta}^{*p}(t,s)-r_{\theta}^{*p}(t-s)
\displaystyle=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}R_{\theta}^{*k}*(R_{\theta}-r_{\theta})*r_{\theta}^{*(p-1-k)}(t,s)
\displaystyle=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\int_{s}^{t}\mathrm{d}t_{1}\int_{s}^{t_{1}}\mathrm{d}t_{2}\,R_{\theta}^{*k}(t,t_{1})[R_{\theta}-r_{\theta}](t_{1},t_{2})r_{\theta}^{*(p-1-k)}(t_{2},s).
By Lemma 4.1, we have |[R_{\theta}-r_{\theta}](t_{1},t_{2})|\leq Ce^{-ct_{2}}\leq Ce^{-cs} . Then,
together with (4.42) and (4.47),
this gives
\displaystyle|R_{\theta}^{*p}(t,s)-r_{\theta}^{*p}(t-s)|
\displaystyle\leq\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}Ce^{-cs}\int_{s}^{t}\mathrm{d}t_{1}\int_{s}^{t_{1}}\mathrm{d}t_{2}\,|R_{\theta}^{*k}(t,t_{1})|\cdot r_{\theta}^{*(p-1-k)}(t_{2}-s)
\displaystyle\leq C^{\prime}pe^{-cs}(v_{*}-q_{*}+\varepsilon/4)^{p-1}.
Applying again |\kappa_{p}|\leq C^{p} , we then have
\sum_{p=1}^{\max(\delta s,p_{0})}|\kappa_{p+1}|\cdot|R_{\theta}(t,s)^{*p}-r_{\theta}(t-s)^{*p}|\leq Ce^{-cs}\cdot e^{C\max(\delta s,p_{0})}.
This is at most C^{\prime}e^{-(c/2)s} for \delta>0 small enough, and combining with
the above yields
|R_{g}(t,s)-r_{g}(t-s)|\leq Ce^{-cs}.
By this bound, (4.46), and (4.49),
also \int_{0}^{t}|R_{g}(t,s)-r_{g}(t-s)|\mathrm{d}s\leq Ce^{-ct} by
the same argument as following (4.34),
showing all statements of part (a).
Part (b): Recall that
c_{g}(\tau)=\sum_{p,q\geq 0}\kappa_{p+q+2}\,r_{\theta}^{*p}*c_{\theta}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*q}(\tau).
Bounding 0\leq c_{\theta}(\tau)\leq C shows that
0\leq r_{\theta}^{*p}*c_{\theta}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*q}(\tau)\leq C\int r_{\theta}^{*p}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*q}(s)\mathrm{d}s=C(v_{*}-q_{*})^{p+q} ,
so by (4.6), the above series defining
c_{g}(\tau) is absolutely and uniformly convergent over \tau\in\mathbb{R} .
Since each summand is continuous, c_{g}:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R} is continuous.
Write c_{\theta}(\tau)=c_{\theta}^{0}(\tau)+q_{*} . Note that
for the constant function q_{*}(\tau)\equiv q_{*} , we have
\displaystyle\sum_{p,q\geq 0}\kappa_{p+q+2}\,r_{\theta}^{*p}*q_{*}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*q}(\tau)
\displaystyle=\sum_{p,q\geq 0}\kappa_{p+q+2}\cdot q_{*}\int r_{\theta}^{*p}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*q}(s)\mathrm{d}s
\displaystyle=q_{*}\sum_{p,q\geq 0}\kappa_{p+q+2}(v_{*}-q_{*})^{p+q}
\displaystyle=q_{*}\sum_{k\geq 0}\kappa_{k+2}(k+1)(v_{*}-q_{*})^{k}=q_{*}\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}^{\prime}(v_{*}-q_{*}),
where the last identity holds since (4.6) implies
\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}(x)=\sum_{p\geq 0}\kappa_{p+1}x^{p} is absolutely convergent in a
neighborhood of v_{*}-q_{*} . Thus
c_{g}(\tau)=c_{g}^{0}(\tau)+q_{*}\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}^{\prime}(v_{*}-q_{*}),\qquad c_{g}^{0}(\tau):=\sum_{p,q\geq 0}\kappa_{p+q+2}\,r_{\theta}^{*p}*c_{\theta}^{0}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*q}(\tau).
To show exponential decay of c_{g}^{0}(\tau) , fix a constant \delta>0 ,
and recall p_{0} for which (4.45) holds. Then, for summands where p+q\geq\max(\delta\tau,p_{0}) ,
bounding |c_{\theta}^{0}(\tau)|\leq C for all \tau\in\mathbb{R} , we have as above
\displaystyle\sum_{p,q:\,p+q\geq\max(\delta\tau,p_{0})}|\kappa_{p+q+2}|\cdot|[r_{\theta}^{*p}*c_{\theta}^{0}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*q}](\tau)|
\displaystyle\leq C\sum_{p,q:\,p+q\geq\max(\delta\tau,p_{0})}|\kappa_{p+q+2}|\cdot(v_{*}-q_{*})^{p+q}\leq C^{\prime}e^{-c\delta\tau}.
For p+q\leq\max(\delta\tau,p_{0}) ,
applying the bounds |r_{\theta}(\tau)|,|c_{\theta}^{0}(\tau)|\leq Ce^{-c\tau} from
Lemma 4.1 together with (4.40),
\displaystyle\sum_{p,q:\,p+q<\max(\delta\tau,p_{0})}|\kappa_{p+q+2}|\cdot|[r_{\theta}^{*p}*c_{\theta}^{0}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*q}](\tau)|
\displaystyle\hskip 72.26999pt\leq\sum_{p,q:\,p+q<\max(\delta\tau,p_{0})}C^{p+q+1}e^{-c\tau}\leq C^{\prime}e^{-c\tau}\cdot e^{C^{\prime}\max(\delta\tau,p_{0})}.
Choosing \delta>0 small enough and combining with the above shows
\lim_{\tau\to\infty}c_{g}(\tau)=q_{*}\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}^{\prime}(v_{*}-q_{*}) and
|c_{g}(\tau)-q_{*}\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}^{\prime}(v_{*}-q_{*})|=|c_{g}^{0}(\tau)|\leq Ce^{-c\tau}.
To bound |C_{g}(t,s)-c_{g}(t-s)| , identify r_{\theta}(t,s)\equiv r_{\theta}(t-s)
and c_{\theta}(t,s)\equiv c_{\theta}(t-s) , and note that
C_{g}(t,s)-c_{g}(t-s)=\sum_{p,q\geq 0}\kappa_{p+q+2}\big(R_{\theta}^{*p}*C_{\theta}*\bar{R}_{\theta}^{*q}-r_{\theta}^{*p}*c_{\theta}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*q}\big)(t,s).
Fixing a small constant \delta>0 , for summands where p+q\geq\max(\delta\min(s,t),p_{0}) , we may bound |C_{\theta}(t,s)|,|c_{\theta}(t,s)|\leq C and apply (4.42) and (4.47) to get
\sum_{p,q:\,p+q\geq\max(\delta\min(s,t),p_{0})}|\kappa_{p+q+2}|\cdot\big|\big(R_{\theta}^{*p}*C_{\theta}*\bar{R}_{\theta}^{*q}-r_{\theta}^{*p}*c_{\theta}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*q}\big)(t,s)\big|\leq Ce^{-c\delta\min(s,t)}.
For the summands where p+q<\max(\delta\min(s,t),p_{0}) , write
\big(R_{\theta}^{*p}*C_{\theta}*\bar{R}_{\theta}^{*q}-r_{\theta}^{*p}*c_{\theta}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*q}\big)(t,s)=\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{II}+\mathrm{III}
where
\displaystyle\mathrm{I}
\displaystyle=R_{\theta}^{*p}*(C_{\theta}-c_{\theta})*\bar{R}_{\theta}^{*q}(t,s),
\displaystyle\mathrm{II}
\displaystyle=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}R_{\theta}^{*k}*(R_{\theta}-r_{\theta})*r_{\theta}^{*(p-1-k)}*c_{\theta}*\bar{R}_{\theta}^{*q}(t,s),
\displaystyle\mathrm{III}
\displaystyle=\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}r_{\theta}^{*p}*c_{\theta}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*(q-1-k)}*(\bar{R}_{\theta}-\bar{r}_{\theta})*\bar{R}_{\theta}^{*k}(t,s).
For \mathrm{I} , applying |C_{\theta}(t^{\prime},s^{\prime})-c_{\theta}(t^{\prime},s^{\prime})|\leq Ce^{-c\min(s^{\prime},t^{\prime})}
from Lemma 4.1, and (4.40) to bound
|R_{\theta}^{*p}| and |R_{\theta}^{*q}| , we have
\displaystyle|\mathrm{I}|
\displaystyle\leq\int_{0}^{t}\mathrm{d}t^{\prime}\int_{0}^{s}\mathrm{d}s^{\prime}\,|R_{\theta}^{*p}(t,t^{\prime})|\cdot|C_{\theta}(t^{\prime},s^{\prime})-c_{\theta}(t^{\prime},s^{\prime})|\cdot|R_{\theta}^{*q}(s,s^{\prime})|
\displaystyle\leq\int_{0}^{t}\mathrm{d}t^{\prime}\int_{0}^{s}\mathrm{d}s^{\prime}\,Ce^{-c\min(s^{\prime},t^{\prime})}\cdot C^{p+q}e^{-c(t-t^{\prime})-c(s-s^{\prime})}.
Considering separately the regions of integration where \min(s^{\prime},t^{\prime})\geq\frac{1}{2}\min(s,t) , where
s^{\prime}\leq t^{\prime} and s^{\prime}\leq\frac{1}{2}\min(s,t) in which
case s-s^{\prime}\geq\frac{1}{2}\min(s,t) ,
and where t^{\prime}\leq s^{\prime} and t^{\prime}\leq\frac{1}{2}\min(s,t) in which
case t-t^{\prime}\geq\frac{1}{2}\min(s,t) , we get
|\mathrm{I}|\leq C^{p+q}\cdot C^{\prime}e^{-(c/2)\min(s,t)}
For \mathrm{II} , let us apply from Lemma 4.1 that
|(R_{\theta}-r_{\theta})(t,s)|\leq Ce^{-cs} when s\geq 0 ,
and |(R_{\theta}-r_{\theta})(t,s)|=|r_{\theta}(t-s)|\leq C when s<0 .
Let us also apply (4.40) to bound
r_{\theta}^{*(p-1-k)}*c_{\theta}*\bar{R}_{\theta}^{*q} .
Then each term of \mathrm{II} is bounded similarly as
\displaystyle|R_{\theta}^{*k}*(R_{\theta}-r_{\theta})*r_{\theta}^{*(p-1-k)}*c_{\theta}*\bar{R}_{\theta}^{*q}(t,s)|
\displaystyle\leq\int_{0}^{t}\mathrm{d}t_{1}\int_{-\infty}^{t_{1}}\mathrm{d}t_{2}\,|R_{\theta}^{*k}(t,t_{1})|\cdot|(R_{\theta}-r_{\theta})(t_{1},t_{2})|\cdot|r_{\theta}^{*(p-1-k)}*c_{\theta}*\bar{R}_{\theta}^{*q}(t_{2},s)|
\displaystyle\leq\int_{0}^{t}\mathrm{d}t_{1}\int_{-\infty}^{t_{1}}\mathrm{d}t_{2}\,C^{k}e^{-c(t-t_{1})}\cdot Ce^{-c\max(t_{2},0)}\cdot C^{p+q-k}e^{-c|t_{2}-s|}
\displaystyle\leq C^{p+q}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}C^{\prime}e^{-c\max(t_{2},0)-c|t_{2}-s|}\mathrm{d}t_{2}.
Considering separately the regions where t_{2}\leq s/2 and t_{2}>s/2 , this is
at most C^{p+q}\cdot C^{\prime\prime}e^{-(c/2)s} . Thus
|\mathrm{II}|\leq C^{p+q}\cdot p\cdot C^{\prime\prime}e^{-(c/2)s}.
Similarly, we have |\mathrm{III}|\leq C^{p+q}\cdot q\cdot C^{\prime\prime}e^{-(c/2)t} . Combining
these bounds, for some constants C,c>0 ,
|\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{II}+\mathrm{III}|\leq C^{p+q+1}\cdot(p+q+1)\cdot e^{-c\min(s,t)}.
Thus
\displaystyle\sum_{p,q:\,p+q<\max(\delta\min(s,t),p_{0})}|\kappa_{p+q+2}|\cdot\big|\big(R_{\theta}^{*p}*C_{\theta}*\bar{R}_{\theta}^{*q}-r_{\theta}^{*p}*c_{\theta}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*q}\big)(t,s)\big|
\displaystyle\hskip 144.54pt\leq C^{\prime}e^{-c\min(s,t)}\cdot e^{C^{\prime}\max(\delta\min(s,t),p_{0}))},
which is at most C^{\prime\prime}e^{-(c/2)\min(s,t)} for small enough \delta>0 . This
establishes
|C_{g}(t,s)-c_{g}(t-s)|\leq Ce^{-c\min(s,t)},
showing both bounds of (4.10).
Theorem 2.4 implies C_{g} is a positive-semidefinite kernel.
Since c_{g}(\tau)=\lim_{s\to\infty}C_{g}(s+\tau,s) for each fixed \tau\in\mathbb{R} , this implies that c_{g} is symmetric positive-semidefinite
on \mathbb{R} . Since q_{*}\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}^{\prime}(v_{*}-q_{*})=\lim_{\tau\to\infty}c_{g}(\tau) , we then have
q_{*}\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}^{\prime}(v_{*}-q_{*})\geq 0.
Finally, let us check the differentiability of c_{g}^{0}(\tau)=c_{g}(\tau)-q_{*}\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}^{\prime}(v_{*}-q_{*}) ,
the fluctuation-dissipation relation (4.9), and the value of
c_{g}(0) . Analogously to (4.44), c_{g}^{0} is continuously-differentiable
on \mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\} , with derivative
\displaystyle{c_{g}^{0}}^{\prime}(\tau)
\displaystyle=\sum_{p,q\geq 0}\kappa_{p+q+2}(r_{\theta}^{*p}*c_{\theta}^{0}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*q})^{\prime}(\tau)
\displaystyle=\sum_{p\geq 1,\,q\geq 0}\kappa_{p+q+2}\left(r_{\theta}^{*(p-1)}*c_{\theta}^{0}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*q}(\tau)+r_{\theta}^{\prime}*r_{\theta}^{*(p-1)}*c_{\theta}^{0}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*q}(\tau)\right)
(4.50)
\displaystyle\hskip 36.135pt+\sum_{q\geq 1}\kappa_{q+2}\left(c_{\theta}^{0}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*(q-1)}(\tau)+c_{\theta}^{0}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*(q-1)}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{\prime}(\tau)\right)+\kappa_{2}c_{\theta}^{\prime}(\tau).
This holds since the bound 0\leq c_{\theta}(\tau)\leq C
and (4.42)
imply that (4.50) is absolutely and uniformly convergent over
\tau\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\} .
From the existence of c_{\theta}^{\prime}(0^{+}) in Lemma 4.1,
this shows also the existence of c_{g}^{\prime}(0^{+})={c_{g}^{0}}^{\prime}(0^{+}) .
Setting r_{g}(\tau)=0 for \tau<0 and \bar{r}_{g}(\tau)=r_{g}(-\tau) ,
and applying (4.41) and
(4.42), both the series (4.50) and
r_{g}(\tau)=\sum_{p\geq 1}\kappa_{p+1}r_{\theta}^{*p}(\tau),\qquad\bar{r}_{g}(\tau)=\sum_{p\geq 1}\kappa_{p+1}\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*p}(\tau)
are also absolutely convergent in L^{1}(\mathbb{R}) . Then, writing
\mathcal{F}[f](\omega)=\int f(t)e^{-i\omega t}\mathrm{d}t for the Fourier transform
and applying \mathcal{F}[f^{\prime}](\omega)=i\omega\mathcal{F}[f](\omega) on the Sobolev space f\in W^{1,1} , we have
(4.51)
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}[c_{g}^{0}](\omega)
\displaystyle=\sum_{p,q\geq 0}\kappa_{p+q+2}\mathcal{F}[(r_{\theta}^{*p}*c_{\theta}^{0}*\bar{r}_{\theta}^{*q})](\omega)
\displaystyle=\sum_{p,q\geq 0}\kappa_{p+q+2}\mathcal{F}[r_{\theta}](\omega)^{p}\mathcal{F}[c_{\theta}^{0}](\omega)\mathcal{F}[\bar{r}_{\theta}](\omega)^{q}
\displaystyle=\mathcal{F}[c_{\theta}^{0}](\omega)\sum_{k\geq 0}\kappa_{k+2}\frac{\mathcal{F}[r_{\theta}](\omega)^{k+1}-\mathcal{F}[\bar{r}_{\theta}](\omega)^{k+1}}{\mathcal{F}[r_{\theta}](\omega)-\mathcal{F}[\bar{r}_{\theta}](\omega)},
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}[{c_{g}^{0}}^{\prime}](\omega)
\displaystyle=i\omega\mathcal{F}[c_{\theta}^{0}](\omega)\sum_{k\geq 0}\kappa_{k+2}\frac{\mathcal{F}[r_{\theta}](\omega)^{k+1}-\mathcal{F}[\bar{r}_{\theta}](\omega)^{k+1}}{\mathcal{F}[r_{\theta}](\omega)-\mathcal{F}[\bar{r}_{\theta}](\omega)},
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}[r_{g}](\omega)
\displaystyle=\sum_{p\geq 1}\kappa_{p+1}\mathcal{F}[r_{\theta}](\omega)^{p},\qquad\mathcal{F}[\bar{r}_{g}](\omega)=\sum_{p\geq 1}\kappa_{p+1}\mathcal{F}[\bar{r}_{\theta}](\omega)^{p}.
Applying the fluctuation-dissipation relation
c_{\theta}^{\prime}(\tau)={c_{\theta}^{0}}^{\prime}(\tau)={-}r_{\theta}(\tau) from (4.4)
for \tau>0 , we have
\mathcal{F}[r_{\theta}](\omega)=\int_{0}^{\infty}r_{\theta}(\tau)e^{-i\omega\tau}\mathrm{d}\tau=\int_{0}^{\infty}{-}{c_{\theta}^{0}}^{\prime}(\tau)e^{-i\omega\tau}\mathrm{d}\tau=c_{\theta}^{0}(0)-\int_{0}^{\infty}i\omega c_{\theta}^{0}(\tau)e^{-i\omega\tau}\mathrm{d}\tau,
and likewise
\mathcal{F}[\bar{r}_{\theta}](\omega)=\int_{-\infty}^{0}r_{\theta}(-\tau)e^{-i\omega\tau}\mathrm{d}\tau=\int_{-\infty}^{0}{c_{\theta}^{0}}^{\prime}(\tau)e^{-i\omega\tau}\mathrm{d}\tau=c_{\theta}^{0}(0)+\int_{-\infty}^{0}i\omega c_{\theta}^{0}(\tau)e^{-i\omega\tau}\mathrm{d}\tau.
Thus
\mathcal{F}[r_{\theta}](\omega)-\mathcal{F}[\bar{r}_{\theta}](\omega)={-}i\omega\int c_{\theta}^{0}(\tau)e^{-i\omega\tau}\mathrm{d}\tau={-}i\omega\mathcal{F}[c_{\theta}^{0}](\omega).
Applying this above shows
\mathcal{F}[{c_{g}^{0}}^{\prime}](\omega)=-(\mathcal{F}[r_{g}](\omega)-\mathcal{F}[\bar{r}_{g}](\omega))=-\int\operatorname{sign}(\tau)r_{g}(|\tau|)e^{-i\omega\tau}\mathrm{d}\tau.
Thus c_{g}^{\prime}(\tau)={c_{g}^{0}}^{\prime}(\tau)={-}\operatorname{sign}(\tau)r_{g}(|\tau|) for a.e. \tau\in\mathbb{R} .
The continuity of both functions restricted to (0,\infty) , and also
from the right at \tau=0 , implies {-}c_{g}^{\prime}(\tau)=r_{g}(\tau) for \tau>0 and
{-}c_{g}^{\prime}(0^{+})=r_{g}(0) , verifying (4.9). Finally,
recalling that \lim_{\tau\to\infty}c_{g}(\tau)=q_{*}\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}^{\prime}(v_{*}-q_{*}) ,
this implies that
\displaystyle c_{g}(0)-q_{*}\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}^{\prime}(v_{*}-q_{*})
\displaystyle=\int_{0}^{\infty}r_{g}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau
\displaystyle=\sum_{p\geq 1}\kappa_{p+1}\int_{0}^{\infty}r_{\theta}^{*p}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau=\sum_{p\geq 1}\kappa_{p+1}(v_{*}-q_{*})^{p}=\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}(v_{*}-q_{*}).
Since c_{g}:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R} is positive-semidefinite, we must have
\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}(v_{*}-q_{*})=\allowbreak c_{g}(0)-\allowbreak\lim_{\tau\to\infty}c_{g}(\tau)\geq 0.
This shows all statements of part (b).
∎
5. Replica-symmetric overlaps and free energy
In this section, we prove Theorem 2.6 on the asymptotic overlaps
and free energy of the Gibbs measure (2.8).
The argument is to establish a Markovian approximation of the generalized
Langevin
equation (2.2), using the fluctuation-dissipation relation between c_{g},r_{g} in
Lemma 4.2, an approximation of c_{g}^{0}(\tau)=c_{g}(\tau)-\lim_{s\to\infty}c_{g}(s) by the correlation function
of observables of the lifted Markovian process
\boldsymbol{\xi}^{t}=\{\boldsymbol{\theta}^{s}\}_{s\in[t-B,t]} over path histories, a further
approximation of this correlation function by a kernel \tilde{c}_{g} defined
via a finite-dimensional approximation of its infinitesimal generator,
and a stable coupling between the dynamics driven by c_{g}^{0} and \tilde{c}_{g} .
The approximation of c_{g}^{0} (and its derivative {-}r_{g} ) is carried out in the
following lemma.
Lemma 5.1.
Suppose the conditions of Theorem 2.6 hold. Let
v_{*},q_{*},c_{g}(\tau),r_{g}(\tau) be as defined in Lemmas 4.1 and
4.2, and set
c_{g}^{0}(\tau)=c_{g}(\tau)-q_{*}\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}^{\prime}(v_{*}-q_{*}).
Fix any \varepsilon>0 . Then there exists a constant C>0
independent of \varepsilon , and some T_{0}=T_{0}(\varepsilon)>0
and function \ell_{*}:[0,T_{0}]^{2}\to\mathbb{R} , such that the following holds:
For any T>0 and \delta>0 , there exist
m\geq 1 , u_{m}\in\mathbb{R}^{m} , and A_{m}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m} with
A_{m}+A_{m}^{\top} strictly positive definite,
all depending on \delta,T,\varepsilon,T_{0} , such that:
(i)
|u_{m}^{\top}e^{-\tau A_{m}}u_{m}-c_{g}^{0}(\tau)|<\delta for all \tau\in[0,T] .
(ii)
\int_{0}^{\infty}|u_{m}^{\top}A_{m}e^{-\tau A_{m}}u_{m}-r_{g}(\tau)|\mathrm{d}\tau<\delta .
(iii)
\|u_{m}\|_{2}<C .
(iv)
\|e^{-tA_{m}}u_{m}\|_{2}<\varepsilon for all t\geq T_{0} .
(v)
\|(e^{-tA_{m}}-e^{-sA_{m}})u_{m}\|_{2}<C|t-s|^{1/2}+\delta
and \|A_{m}(e^{-tA_{m}}-e^{-sA_{m}})u_{m}\|_{2}<C|t-s|^{1/2}+\delta
for all s,t\in[0,T_{0}] .
(vi)
|u_{m}^{\top}e^{-tA_{m}^{\top}}A_{m}e^{-sA_{m}}u_{m}-\ell_{*}(t,s)|<\delta
for all s,t\in[0,T_{0}] .
We emphasize that for our later coupling argument, it is important that the
constants C,\varepsilon,T_{0} in statements (iii)–(vi) are fixed irrespective of m .
Proof.
We again assume, without loss of generality, that Assumption 4.3
holds. The process \{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}} and conventions
for \langle\cdot\rangle are the same as in the proof
of Lemma 4.1.
Step 1 (Markov semigroup setup):
For a value B=B(n)>0 to be determined, let
\mathcal{S}=C([-B,0],\mathbb{R}^{n}) denote the space of continuous bounded
\mathbb{R}^{n} -valued functions on [-B,0] . We denote elements of this space by
\boldsymbol{\xi}\in\mathcal{S} , indexed as \boldsymbol{\xi}=\{\boldsymbol{\xi}_{\tau}\}_{\tau\in[-B,0]} .
\mathcal{S} is equipped with the norm
\|\boldsymbol{\xi}\|=\sup_{\tau\in[-B,0]}\|\boldsymbol{\xi}_{\tau}\|_{2}
and its associated Borel sigma-algebra. Denote
\boldsymbol{\xi}^{t}=\{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t+\tau}\}_{\tau\in[-B,0]},\text{ i.e. }\boldsymbol{\xi}_{\tau}^{t}=\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t+\tau}\text{ for }\tau\in[-B,0].
We use subscripts to index elements of \mathcal{S}
and superscripts to index the process \{\boldsymbol{\xi}^{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}} on \mathcal{S} .
Let \nu be the law of \boldsymbol{\xi}^{0}=\{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{\tau}\}_{\tau\in[-B,0]}
on \mathcal{S} . Then \{\boldsymbol{\xi}^{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}} is a
\mathcal{S} -valued Markov process with stationary law \nu .
Let L^{2}(\mu_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}) and L^{2}(\nu) be the spaces of
Borel-measurable functions f_{0}:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}^{n} and
f:\mathcal{S}\to\mathbb{R}^{n} , respectively, such that
\|f_{0}\|_{L^{2}}^{2}:=\frac{1}{n}\,\mathbb{E}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}\sim\mu_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}}\|f_{0}(\boldsymbol{\theta})\|_{2}^{2}<\infty,\qquad\|f\|_{L^{2}}^{2}:=\frac{1}{n}\,\mathbb{E}_{\boldsymbol{\xi}\sim\nu}\|f(\boldsymbol{\xi})\|_{2}^{2}<\infty,
and write \langle\cdot\rangle_{L^{2}} for the associated inner-products.
Consider the Markov semigroup \{P_{t}\}_{t\geq 0} of
bounded operators on L^{2}(\nu) given by
P_{t}f(\boldsymbol{\xi})=\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{\xi}^{t})\mid\boldsymbol{\xi}^{0}=\boldsymbol{\xi}].
Note that for any f\in L^{2}(\nu) , we have the contractivity property
\|P_{t}f\|_{L^{2}}\leq\|f\|_{L^{2}} by Jensen’s inequality. Furthermore,
this semigroup is strongly continuous in the sense
(5.1)
\lim_{t\to 0^{+}}\|P_{t}f-f\|_{L^{2}}=0\text{ for each fixed }f\in L^{2}(\nu).
Indeed, as t\to 0^{+} , we have \boldsymbol{\xi}^{t}\to\boldsymbol{\xi}^{0} in
\mathcal{S}=C([-B,0],\mathbb{R}^{n}) by the uniform continuity of sample paths of
\{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}} on compact intervals. Thus if
f:\mathcal{S}\to\mathbb{R}^{n} is continuous and bounded, then by dominated convergence,
\lim_{t\to 0^{+}}\|P_{t}f-f\|_{L^{2}}^{2}=\lim_{t\to 0^{+}}\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}\|\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{\xi}^{t})\mid\boldsymbol{\xi}^{0}]-f(\boldsymbol{\xi}^{0})\|_{2}^{2}\leq\lim_{t\to 0^{+}}\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}\|f(\boldsymbol{\xi}^{t})-f(\boldsymbol{\xi}^{0})\|_{2}^{2}=0.
As \mathcal{S} is separable,
the space of such continuous and bounded functions on \mathcal{S}
is dense in L^{2}(\nu) . Then, since P_{t} is also contractive,
this implies the strong continuity (5.1).
Define the generator -A:D(A)\to L^{2}(\nu) for \{P_{t}\}_{t\geq 0} by
-Af=\lim_{t\to 0^{+}}\frac{1}{t}(P_{t}f-f)
where D(A)\subset L^{2}(\nu) is the domain where this limit exists in
L^{2}(\nu) . Let r_{g}^{B}:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R} be a compactly supported,
smooth approximation of r_{g} such that
r_{g}^{B}(\tau)=\begin{cases}r_{g}(\tau)&\text{ for }\tau\in[0,B-1],\\
0&\text{ for }\tau\geq B,\end{cases}
and |r_{g}^{B}(\tau)|\leq|r_{g}(\tau)|
and |{r_{g}^{B}}^{\prime}(\tau)|\leq C|r_{g}^{\prime}(\tau)| for a constant C>0 and
all \tau\geq 0 . Consider the function f_{B}\in L^{2}(\nu) given by
(5.2)
f_{B}(\boldsymbol{\xi})=\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\xi}_{0}-\int_{-B}^{0}r_{g}^{B}(-s)\boldsymbol{\xi}_{s}\mathrm{d}s-\mathbb{E}_{\boldsymbol{\xi}\sim\nu}\left[\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\xi}_{0}-\int_{-B}^{0}r^{B}_{g}(-s)\boldsymbol{\xi}_{s}\mathrm{d}s\right].
We claim that f_{B}\in D(A) . To see this, let
P_{t}^{\theta}f_{0}(\boldsymbol{\theta})=\mathbb{E}[f_{0}(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t})\mid\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}=\boldsymbol{\theta}] denote the Markov diffusion semigroup on L^{2}(\mu_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}) ,
and let
(5.3)
-A^{\theta}f_{0}(\boldsymbol{\theta})=\Big((\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\theta}-U^{\prime}(\boldsymbol{\theta}))^{\top}\nabla f_{0,i}(\boldsymbol{\theta})+\operatorname{Tr}\nabla^{2}f_{0,i}(\boldsymbol{\theta})\Big)_{i=1}^{n}
denote its generator with domain D(A^{\theta})\subset L^{2}(\mu_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}) . Denote f_{B,0}(\boldsymbol{\theta})=\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\theta} , and write c_{0} for the
last constant term of (5.2) (not depending on \boldsymbol{\xi} ). Then
\displaystyle P_{t}f_{B}(\boldsymbol{\xi})
\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[f_{B,0}(\boldsymbol{\xi}_{0}^{t})\mid\boldsymbol{\xi}^{0}=\boldsymbol{\xi}]-\int_{-B}^{0}r_{g}^{B}({-}s)\mathbb{E}[\boldsymbol{\xi}_{s}^{t}\mid\boldsymbol{\xi}^{0}=\boldsymbol{\xi}]\mathrm{d}s-c_{0}
\displaystyle=P_{t}^{\theta}f_{B,0}(\boldsymbol{\xi}_{0})-\int_{\max(-t,-B)}^{0}r_{g}^{B}({-}s)\mathbb{E}[\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t+s}\mid\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}=\boldsymbol{\xi}_{0}]\mathrm{d}s
\displaystyle\quad-\int_{-B}^{\max(-t,-B)}r_{g}^{B}({-}s)\boldsymbol{\xi}_{t+s}\mathrm{d}s-c_{0}.
For t\in(0,B) , we have
\displaystyle\frac{1}{t}(P_{t}f_{B}(\boldsymbol{\xi})-f_{B}(\boldsymbol{\xi}))
\displaystyle=\frac{1}{t}(P_{t}^{\theta}f_{B,0}(\boldsymbol{\xi}_{0})-f_{B,0}(\boldsymbol{\xi}_{0}))-\frac{1}{t}\int_{-t}^{0}r_{g}^{B}({-}s)\mathbb{E}[\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t+s}\mid\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}=\boldsymbol{\xi}_{0}]\mathrm{d}s
\displaystyle-\frac{1}{t}\left(\int_{-B+t}^{0}(r_{g}^{B}(t-s)-r_{g}^{B}({-}s))\boldsymbol{\xi}_{s}\mathrm{d}s\right)+\frac{1}{t}\int_{-B}^{-B+t}r_{g}^{B}({-}s)\boldsymbol{\xi}_{s}\mathrm{d}s.
Under the condition that Assumption 2.2 holds for {-}U^{\prime} ,
f_{B,0} belongs to D(A^{\theta}) , so
\lim_{t\to 0^{+}}\frac{1}{t}(P_{t}^{\theta}f_{B,0}-f_{B,0})(\boldsymbol{\theta})={-}A^{\theta}f_{B,0}(\boldsymbol{\theta})=\mathbf{X}(\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\theta}-U^{\prime}(\boldsymbol{\theta})).
Pointwise over \boldsymbol{\xi}\in\mathcal{S} , since \boldsymbol{\xi}_{s} and
\mathbb{E}[\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{s}\mid\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}=\boldsymbol{\xi}_{0}] are
continuous in s and r_{g}^{B}(s) is continuously-differentiable with
r_{g}^{B}(B)=0 , we have
\displaystyle\lim_{t\to 0^{+}}\Bigg({-}\frac{1}{t}\int_{-t}^{0}r_{g}^{B}({-}s)\mathbb{E}[\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t+s}\mid\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}=\boldsymbol{\xi}_{0}]\mathrm{d}s-\frac{1}{t}\left(\int_{-B+t}^{0}(r_{g}^{B}(t-s)-r_{g}^{B}({-}s))\boldsymbol{\xi}_{s}\mathrm{d}s\right)
\displaystyle\hskip 36.135pt+\frac{1}{t}\int_{-B}^{-B+t}r_{g}^{B}({-}s)\boldsymbol{\xi}_{s}\mathrm{d}s\Bigg)={-}r_{g}^{B}(0)\boldsymbol{\xi}_{0}-\int_{-B}^{0}{r_{g}^{B}}^{\prime}(s)\boldsymbol{\xi}_{s}\mathrm{d}s+0.
By dominated convergence, this holds also as functions of \boldsymbol{\xi} in
L^{2}(\nu) . Thus {-}Af_{B} exists in L^{2}(\nu) , and is given explicitly by
(5.4)
-Af_{B}(\boldsymbol{\xi})=\lim_{t\to 0^{+}}\frac{1}{t}(P_{t}f_{B}(\boldsymbol{\xi})-f_{B}(\boldsymbol{\xi}))=\mathbf{X}(\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\xi}_{0}-U^{\prime}(\boldsymbol{\xi}_{0}))-r_{g}^{B}(0)\boldsymbol{\xi}_{0}-\int_{-B}^{0}{r_{g}^{B}}^{\prime}(s)\boldsymbol{\xi}_{s}\mathrm{d}s.
This checks that f_{B}\in D(A) .
Step 2 (semigroup estimates): Let us establish bounds independent of
n,B for the quantities
\displaystyle\|P_{t}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}},\quad\|Af_{B}\|_{L^{2}},\quad\|(P_{t}-P_{s})f_{B}\|_{L^{2}},\quad\|(P_{t}-P_{s})Af_{B}\|_{L^{2}}.
For convenience, define
(5.5)
\displaystyle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{t}
\displaystyle=\mathbf{X}\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}-\int_{-\infty}^{t}r_{g}^{B}(t-s)\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{s}\mathrm{d}s,
(5.6)
\displaystyle\tilde{\mathbf{a}}_{B}^{t}
\displaystyle=\mathbf{X}(\mathbf{X}\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}-U^{\prime}(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}))-r_{g}(0)\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}-\int_{-\infty}^{t}{r_{g}^{B}}^{\prime}(t-s)\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{s}\mathrm{d}s,
and recall the notation \langle\cdot\rangle for the
expectation over \{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}} conditional on \mathbf{X} . Then
(5.7)
f_{B}(\boldsymbol{\xi}^{t})=\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{t}-\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{0}\rangle,\qquad{-}Af_{B}(\boldsymbol{\xi}^{t})=\tilde{\mathbf{a}}_{B}^{t}.
For \|P_{t}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}} , write
\displaystyle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{t}-\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{0}\rangle
\displaystyle=\mathbf{g}_{B,1}^{t}+\mathbf{g}_{B,2}^{t},
\displaystyle\mathbf{g}_{B,1}^{t}
\displaystyle=\mathbf{X}(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}-\langle\boldsymbol{\theta}\rangle)-\int_{0}^{\min(t/2,B)}r_{g}^{B}(s)(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t-s}-\langle\boldsymbol{\theta}\rangle)\mathrm{d}s,
\displaystyle\mathbf{g}_{B,2}^{t}
\displaystyle={-}\int_{\min(t/2,B)}^{B}r_{g}^{B}(s)(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t-s}-\langle\boldsymbol{\theta}\rangle)\mathrm{d}s\quad\text{ if }t/2<B,\text{ or }\mathbf{g}_{B,2}^{t}=0\text{ otherwise}.
When \mathbf{g}_{B,2}^{t}\neq 0 , we may bound
\displaystyle\left\langle\frac{1}{n}\,\|\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{g}_{B,2}^{t}\mid\mathbf{X},\{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{r}\}_{r\leq 0}]\|_{2}^{2}\right\rangle\leq\frac{1}{n}\,\langle\|\mathbf{g}_{B,2}^{t}\|_{2}^{2}\rangle
\displaystyle\leq\int_{\min(t/2,B)}^{B}\mathrm{d}t^{\prime}\int_{\min(t/2,B)}^{B}\mathrm{d}s^{\prime}\,|r_{g}^{B}(t^{\prime})|\,|r_{g}^{B}(s^{\prime})|\,\frac{1}{n}\Big|\langle(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t-t^{\prime}}-\langle\boldsymbol{\theta}\rangle)^{\top}(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{s-s^{\prime}}-\langle\boldsymbol{\theta}\rangle)\rangle\Big|
\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{n}\langle\|\boldsymbol{\theta}\|_{2}^{2}\rangle\left(\int_{t/2}^{\infty}|r_{g}(t^{\prime})|\mathrm{d}t^{\prime}\right)^{2}.
Applying (4.11) and the exponential bound for r_{g}
from Lemma 4.2,
(5.8)
\sup_{B>0}\left\langle\frac{1}{n}\|\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{g}_{B,2}^{t}\mid\mathbf{X},\{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{r}\}_{r\leq 0}]\|_{2}^{2}\right\rangle^{1/2}\leq Ce^{-ct}\text{ for all }t\geq 0.
For \mathbf{g}_{B,1}^{t} , recall that for each t\geq 0 ,
there exists a coupling (4.20)
of (\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0},\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}) with \boldsymbol{\theta}\sim\mu_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}
for which \boldsymbol{\theta} is independent of \tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0} and
\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}[\|\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}-\boldsymbol{\theta}\|_{2}^{2}\mid\mathbf{X}]\leq Ce^{-ct} .
Then by Jensen’s inequality, also
\frac{1}{n}\langle\|\mathbb{E}[\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}\mid\mathbf{X},\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}]-\langle\boldsymbol{\theta}\rangle\|_{2}^{2}\rangle\leq Ce^{-ct} for all t\geq 0 . Hence
\displaystyle\left\langle\frac{1}{n}\,\|\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{g}_{B,1}^{t}\mid\mathbf{X},\{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{r}\}_{r\leq 0}]\|_{2}^{2}\right\rangle
\displaystyle=\left\langle\frac{1}{n}\,\left\|\mathbf{X}(\mathbb{E}[\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}\mid\mathbf{X},\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}]-\langle\boldsymbol{\theta}\rangle)-\int_{0}^{\min(t/2,B)}r_{g}^{B}(s)(\mathbb{E}[\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t-s}\mid\mathbf{X},\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}]-\langle\boldsymbol{\theta}\rangle)\mathrm{d}s\right\|_{2}^{2}\right\rangle
\displaystyle\leq\frac{C}{n}\,\langle\|\mathbb{E}[\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}\mid\mathbf{X},\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}]-\langle\boldsymbol{\theta}\rangle\|_{2}^{2}\rangle+\frac{C}{n}\sup_{s\in[t/2,t]}\langle\|\mathbb{E}[\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{s}\mid\mathbf{X},\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}]-\langle\boldsymbol{\theta}\rangle\|_{2}^{2}\rangle\left(\int_{0}^{\infty}|r_{g}(s)|\,\mathrm{d}s\right)^{2}
\displaystyle\leq C^{\prime}e^{-c^{\prime}t}.
Thus
(5.9)
\sup_{B>0}\left\langle\frac{1}{n}\|\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{g}_{B,1}^{t}\mid\mathbf{X},\{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{r}\}_{r\leq 0}]\|_{2}^{2}\right\rangle^{1/2}\leq Ce^{-ct}\text{ for all }t\geq 0.
Combining (5.8) and (5.9), for some constants C,c>0 ,
(5.10)
\sup_{B>0}\|P_{t}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}\leq Ce^{-ct}\text{ for all }t\geq 0.
For \|Af_{B}\|_{L^{2}} ,
by (4.11) and integrability of |r_{g}^{\prime}| shown in
Lemma 4.2, for a constant C>0 we have similarly
(5.11)
\displaystyle\sup_{B>0}\|Af_{B}\|_{L^{2}}=\sup_{B>0}\left\langle\frac{1}{n}\|\tilde{\mathbf{a}}_{B}^{0}\|_{2}^{2}\right\rangle^{1/2}\leq C.
For \|(P_{t}-P_{s})f_{B}\|_{L^{2}} and \|(P_{t}-P_{s})Af_{B}\|_{L^{2}} ,
note that (4.11)
and (4.37) imply
(5.12)
\frac{1}{n}\langle\|\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{\tau}-\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}\|_{2}^{2}\rangle\leq C\min(\tau,1)\text{ for all }\tau\geq 0.
Then also by the integrability of |r_{g}| ,
\displaystyle\sup_{B>0}\|(P_{s+\tau}-P_{s})f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}\leq\sup_{B>0}\left\langle\frac{1}{n}\|\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{\tau}-\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{0}\|_{2}^{2}\right\rangle^{1/2}
\displaystyle\leq\sup_{B>0}\left\langle\frac{1}{n}\|\mathbf{X}(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{\tau}-\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0})\|_{2}^{2}\right\rangle^{1/2}+\left\langle\frac{1}{n}\left\|\int_{0}^{\infty}r_{g}^{B}(s)(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{\tau-s}-\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{-s})\mathrm{d}s\right\|_{2}^{2}\right\rangle^{1/2}
(5.13)
\displaystyle\leq C\min(\tau^{1/2},1)\text{ for all }s,\tau\geq 0.
Similarly by the integrability of |r_{g}^{\prime}| ,
(5.14)
\sup_{B>0}\|(P_{s+\tau}-P_{s})Af_{B}\|_{L^{2}}\leq\sup_{B>0}\left\langle\frac{1}{n}\|\tilde{\mathbf{a}}_{B}^{\tau}-\tilde{\mathbf{a}}_{B}^{0}\|_{2}^{2}\right\rangle^{1/2}\leq C\min(\tau^{1/2},1)\text{ for all }s,\tau\geq 0.
Step 3 (diffusion approximation of c_{g}^{0} and r_{g} ): We claim that for any
sequence B(n) satisfying B(n)\to\infty as n\to\infty , and for
any T>0 ,
(5.15)
\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\left|c_{g}^{0}(\tau)-\left(\frac{1}{n}\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{0}\rangle-\frac{1}{n}\|\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{0}\rangle\|_{2}^{2}\right)\right|=0\text{ a.s.},
(5.16)
\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\left|r_{g}(\tau)+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\left(\frac{1}{n}\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{0}\rangle\right)\right|=0\text{ a.s.}
To show this claim, observe that
Theorem 2.4(c) and Lemma 4.2 imply that
(5.17)
c_{g}(\tau)=\lim_{t\to\infty}C_{g}(t+\tau,t)=\lim_{t\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\,\langle\mathbf{g}^{t+\tau\top}\mathbf{g}^{t}\rangle\text{ a.s.}
where here and below, all limits in n exist a.s. over (\mathbf{X},\boldsymbol{\theta}^{0}) .
First fixing some constant B>0 , define for t\geq B
\mathbf{g}_{B}^{t}=\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\theta}^{t}-\int_{-\infty}^{t}r_{g}^{B}(t-s)\boldsymbol{\theta}^{s}\mathrm{d}s.
Denote \Delta_{B}(t,s)=R_{g}(t,s)-r_{g}^{B}(t-s) for s\in[0,t] .
By the same argument as (4.37), using
(4.13) to bound \frac{1}{n}\langle\|\boldsymbol{\theta}^{t}\|_{2}^{2}\rangle , we have
(5.18)
\frac{1}{n}\langle\|\boldsymbol{\theta}^{t}-\boldsymbol{\theta}^{s}\|_{2}^{2}\rangle\leq C(e^{C(t-s)}-1)\text{ for all }t\geq s\geq 0.
This equicontinuity and Theorem 2.4(c) imply, for any t\geq 0 ,
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{s\in[0,t]}\left|\frac{1}{n}\boldsymbol{\theta}^{t\top}\boldsymbol{\theta}^{s}-C_{\theta}(t,s)\right|=0\text{ a.s.}
Then for any t\geq B ,
\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\langle\|\mathbf{g}^{t}-\mathbf{g}_{B}^{t}\|^{2}\rangle
\displaystyle=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\left\langle\left\|\int_{0}^{t}\Delta_{B}(t,s)\boldsymbol{\theta}^{s}\mathrm{d}s\right\|^{2}\right\rangle
\displaystyle=\int_{0}^{t}\mathrm{d}s\int_{0}^{t}\mathrm{d}s^{\prime}\Delta_{B}(t,s)\Delta_{B}(t,s^{\prime})C_{\theta}(s,s^{\prime})\text{
a.s.}
Note that \Delta_{B}(t,s)=R_{g}(t,s) for s>t-B+1 .
Then applying the properties for C_{\theta},c_{\theta},R_{g},r_{g}
in Lemmas 4.1 and 4.2,
it is readily checked that for any fixed B>0 :
\displaystyle\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{0}^{t}\mathrm{d}s\int_{0}^{t}\mathrm{d}s^{\prime}\Delta_{B}(t,s)\Delta_{B}(t,s^{\prime})C_{\theta}(s,s^{\prime})
\displaystyle=\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{0}^{t-B+1}\mathrm{d}s\int_{0}^{t-B+1}\mathrm{d}s^{\prime}(R_{g}(t,s)-r_{g}^{B}(t-s))(R_{g}(t,s^{\prime})-r_{g}^{B}(t-s^{\prime}))C_{\theta}(s,s^{\prime})
\displaystyle=\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{B-1}^{t}\mathrm{d}s\int_{B-1}^{t}\mathrm{d}s^{\prime}(R_{g}(t,t-s)-r_{g}^{B}(s))(R_{g}(t,t-s^{\prime})-r_{g}^{B}(s^{\prime}))C_{\theta}(t-s,t-s^{\prime})
\displaystyle=\int_{B-1}^{\infty}\mathrm{d}s\int_{B-1}^{\infty}\mathrm{d}s^{\prime}\,(r_{g}(s)-r_{g}^{B}(s))(r_{g}(s^{\prime})-r_{g}^{B}(s^{\prime}))c_{\theta}(s-s^{\prime}).
Then by the exponential bound for r_{g} in Lemma 4.2, also
\displaystyle\lim_{B\to\infty}\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{0}^{t}\mathrm{d}s\int_{0}^{t}\mathrm{d}s^{\prime}\Delta_{B}(t,s)\Delta_{B}(t,s^{\prime})C_{\theta}(s,s^{\prime})=0.
This shows that
\lim_{B\to\infty}\lim_{t\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\langle\|\mathbf{g}^{t}-\mathbf{g}_{B}^{t}\|_{2}^{2}\rangle=0 a.s.
Applying this bound, (5.17), and Cauchy-Schwarz, we have
(5.19)
\displaystyle\left|c_{g}(\tau)-\lim_{t\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\langle\mathbf{g}_{B}^{t+\tau\top}\mathbf{g}_{B}^{t}\rangle\right|=\left|\lim_{t\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\langle\mathbf{g}^{t+\tau\top}\mathbf{g}^{t}\rangle-\frac{1}{n}\langle\mathbf{g}_{B}^{t+\tau\top}\mathbf{g}_{B}^{t}\rangle\right|\leq o_{B}(1)\text{
a.s.}
where here and below, o_{B}(1) is a constant bound not depending on n,\tau
and vanishing as B\to\infty .
For t>B , Assumption 2.5 implies
there exists a coupling of
(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{0},\boldsymbol{\theta}^{t-B}) with \tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{-B}
having law \mu_{\mathrm{Gibbs}} conditional on \boldsymbol{\theta}^{0} , for which
\frac{1}{n}\,\mathbb{E}[\|\boldsymbol{\theta}^{t-B}-\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{-B}\|_{2}^{2}\mid\mathbf{X},\boldsymbol{\theta}^{0}]\leq Ce^{-ct}.
Define from this coupling of \boldsymbol{\theta}^{t-B} and \tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{-B} a coupling
of \{\boldsymbol{\theta}^{t-B+s}\}_{s\in[0,B+\tau]} and
\{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{-B+s}\}_{s\in[0,B+\tau]} where both processes are driven
by the same Brownian motion. Then by Grönwall’s inequality,
\|\boldsymbol{\theta}^{t-B+s}-\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{-B+s}\|_{2}\leq e^{Cs}\|\boldsymbol{\theta}^{t-B}-\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{-B}\|_{2}\text{ for all }s\in[0,B+\tau].
Thus for any fixed B>0 and \tau>0 ,
there exists a constant C(B,\tau)>0 such that also
\sup_{s\in[0,B+\tau]}\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}[\|\boldsymbol{\theta}^{t-B+s}-\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{-B+s}\|_{2}^{2}\mid\mathbf{X},\boldsymbol{\theta}^{0}]\leq C(B,\tau)e^{-ct}.
This implies from the definitions of \mathbf{g}_{B}^{t} and \tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{t} that
\lim_{t\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\left|\frac{1}{n}\,\langle\mathbf{g}_{B}^{t+\tau\top}\mathbf{g}_{B}^{t}\rangle-\frac{1}{n}\,\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{0}\rangle\right|=0,
so (5.19) implies
(5.20)
\sup_{\tau\geq 0}\left|c_{g}(\tau)-\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\,\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{0}\rangle\right|\leq o_{B}(1)\text{ a.s.}
Since (5.20) implies that the almost-sure limit
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\,\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{0}\rangle converges uniformly to
c_{g}(\tau) as B\to\infty , we have
(5.21)
\displaystyle q_{*}\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}^{\prime}(v_{*}-q_{*})=\lim_{\tau\to\infty}c_{g}(\tau)
\displaystyle=\lim_{\tau\to\infty}\lim_{B\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\,\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{0}\rangle
\displaystyle=\lim_{B\to\infty}\lim_{\tau\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\,\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{0}\rangle\text{ a.s.}
Now let \{\check{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}} be a second diffusion following
(2.11) with equilibrium
initial state \check{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{0}\sim\mu_{\mathrm{Gibbs}} . Again fix B>0 , and
consider \tau>B . Applying again
Assumption 2.5 and the same coupling argument as above,
there exists a coupling of the laws of \{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{\tau-B+s}\}_{s\in[0,B]} and \{\check{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{\tau-B+s}\}_{s\in[0,B]}
conditional on \{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}\}_{t\leq 0} ,
where \{\check{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{\tau-B+s}\}_{s\in[0,B]} is independent of
\{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}\}_{t\leq 0} , for which
\sup_{s\in[0,B]}\frac{1}{n}\,\mathbb{E}[\|\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{\tau-B+s}-\check{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{\tau-B+s}\|_{2}^{2}\mid\mathbf{X}]\leq Ce^{-c\tau}.
Letting \{\check{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}} be the copy of \{\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}} defined from \{\check{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}} ,
this implies by Cauchy-Schwarz that
\lim_{\tau\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\left|\frac{1}{n}\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{0}\rangle-\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}[\check{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{0}\mid\mathbf{X}]\right|=0.
Here \mathbb{E}[\check{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{0}\mid\mathbf{X}]=\|\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{0}\rangle\|_{2}^{2} since
\check{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{\tau} is a function of \{\check{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{\tau-B+s}\}_{s\in[0,B]} , \tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{0} is a function of \{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}\}_{t\leq 0} , and
these are independent. Then, applying this to (5.21), we have
(5.22)
\left|q_{*}\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}^{\prime}(v_{*}-q_{*})-\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\|\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{0}\rangle\|_{2}^{2}\right|\leq o_{B}(1)\text{ a.s.}
For any fixed B>0 and B(n) satisfying B(n)\to\infty as n\to\infty ,
\displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\langle\|\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{\tau}-\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{\tau}\|_{2}^{2}\rangle
\displaystyle=\frac{1}{n}\,\left\langle\left\|\int_{-\infty}^{\tau}(r_{g}^{B}(\tau-s)-r_{g}^{B(n)}(\tau-s))\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{s}\mathrm{d}s\right\|_{2}^{2}\right\rangle
\displaystyle\leq C\left(\int_{B-1}^{\infty}|r_{g}(s)|\mathrm{d}s\right)^{2}\cdot\frac{1}{n}\langle\|\boldsymbol{\theta}\|^{2}\rangle
which is uniformly bounded by (4.11)
and tends to 0 as B\to\infty . Thus
\displaystyle\sup_{\tau\geq 0}\left|\frac{1}{n}\,\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{0}\rangle-\frac{1}{n}\,\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{0}\rangle\right|
\displaystyle\leq o_{B}(1),
\displaystyle\sup_{\tau\geq 0}\left|\frac{1}{n}\|\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B}^{0}\rangle\|_{2}^{2}-\frac{1}{n}\|\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{0}\rangle\|_{2}^{2}\right|
\displaystyle\leq o_{B}(1).
Combining with (5.20) and (5.21)
and noting that the fixed value B>0 may be taken arbitrarily large, this shows
(5.23)
c_{g}^{0}(\tau)=c_{g}(\tau)-q_{*}\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}^{\prime}(v_{*}-q_{*})=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\,\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{0}\rangle-\frac{1}{n}\|\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{0}\rangle\|_{2}^{2}\text{ a.s.}
The bound (5.13) implies that
for all \tau,\tau^{\prime}\in\mathbb{R} and n\geq 1 ,
\left|\frac{1}{n}\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{0}\rangle-\frac{1}{n}\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{\tau^{\prime}\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{0}\rangle\right|\leq C|\tau-\tau^{\prime}|^{1/2}.
Then \tau\mapsto\frac{1}{n}\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{0}\rangle
is uniformly equicontinuous for all n , so the convergence in
(5.23) is
uniform over any compact interval [0,T] ,
establishing the claim (5.15) for c_{g}^{0} .
To show the second claim (5.16) for r_{g} ,
note that Lemma 4.2 shows r_{g}(\tau)={-}{c_{g}^{0}}^{\prime}(\tau) . Using
B=B(n) to define the preceding semigroup \{P_{t}\}_{t\geq 0} on L^{2}(\nu)
in Step 1, the identities (5.7) imply that
\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\,\frac{1}{n}\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{0}\rangle=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\langle f_{B(n)},P_{\tau}f_{B(n)}\rangle_{L^{2}}={-}\langle f_{B(n)},P_{\tau}Af_{B(n)}\rangle_{L^{2}}=\frac{1}{n}\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{0\top}\tilde{\mathbf{a}}_{B(n)}^{\tau}\rangle.
The bound (5.14) implies that this is also uniformly
equicontinuous in \tau for all n . Then by (5.15) and
Arzelà-Ascoli, almost surely
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\left|{c_{g}^{0}}^{\prime}(\tau)-\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\,\frac{1}{n}\langle\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{\tau\top}\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_{B(n)}^{0}\rangle\right|=0.
This shows (5.16).
Step 4 (semigroup regularization):
Take any B(n) such that B(n)\to\infty as n\to\infty .
Henceforth, we define the semigroup \{P_{t}\}_{t\geq 0} with this B(n) and
write simply B\equiv B(n) . For the given value of
\varepsilon in the lemma, let T_{0}=T_{0}(\varepsilon)>0 be large enough such that
(5.10) ensures
(5.24)
\|P_{T_{0}}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}<\varepsilon/3.
The bounds
(5.10), (5.11),
(5.13), and (5.14) imply
that almost surely, \langle P_{t}f_{B},P_{s}Af_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}
is uniformly bounded and uniformly equicontinuous over (t,s) for all n .
Hence along a subsequence of n ,
there exists a limit function \ell_{*}:[0,T_{0}]^{2}\to\mathbb{R}
(possibly random, depending on the infinite sequence of realizations
\mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n} as n\to\infty ) for which
(5.25)
\sup_{s,t\in[0,T_{0}]}|\langle P_{t}f_{B},P_{s}Af_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}-\ell_{*}(t,s)|\to 0.
Now let \delta>0 and T>0 be as given in the lemma. For a sufficiently
small regularization parameter \rho=\rho(\varepsilon,T_{0},\delta,T)>0 to be
determined, define
A^{\rho}=A+\rho\,\mathrm{Id},\qquad P_{t}^{\rho}=e^{-\rho t}P_{t}.
Note that {-}A^{\rho} is then the generator of the regularized semigroup
\{P_{t}^{\rho}\}_{t\geq 0} on L^{2}(\nu) , with the same domain D(A^{\rho})=D(A) .
(Here P_{t}^{\rho} no longer preserves constant functions, which no longer
belong to the kernel of A^{\rho} , but this will be irrelevant for the rest of
the analysis.) Then we have
\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\langle f_{B},P_{t}^{\rho}f_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}={-}\langle f_{B},P_{t}^{\rho}A^{\rho}f_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}={-}e^{-\rho t}\Big(\langle f_{B},P_{t}Af_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}+\rho\langle f_{B},P_{t}f_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}\Big).
Define correspondingly
c_{g}^{\rho}(\tau)=e^{-\rho\tau}c_{g}^{0}(\tau),\qquad r_{g}^{\rho}(\tau)={-}(c_{g}^{\rho})^{\prime}(\tau)=e^{-\rho\tau}(r_{g}(\tau)+\rho c_{g}^{0}(\tau)),
where the last equality uses {-}{c_{g}^{0}}^{\prime}(\tau)=r_{g}(\tau) .
Then (5.15) and (5.16) imply also, for any fixed
\rho>0 and T>0 , almost surely
(5.26)
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}|r_{g}^{\rho}(\tau)-\langle f_{B},P_{\tau}^{\rho}A^{\rho}f_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}|=0.
Note that
\int_{0}^{\infty}|r_{g}^{\rho}(\tau)-r_{g}(\tau)|\,\mathrm{d}\tau\leq\int_{0}^{\infty}(1-e^{-\rho\tau})|r_{g}(\tau)|\mathrm{d}\tau+\int_{0}^{\infty}\rho e^{-\rho\tau}|c_{g}^{0}(\tau)|\mathrm{d}\tau.
Lemma 4.2 shows that both |r_{g}|,|c_{g}^{0}| are integrable, so
by dominated convergence, this approaches to 0 as \rho\to 0 . Thus, for
all small enough \rho , we have
(5.27)
\int_{0}^{\infty}|r_{g}^{\rho}(\tau)-r_{g}(\tau)|\,\mathrm{d}\tau<\delta/8.
Given any \rho>0 , we may pick T(\rho)>0 large enough such that
(5.28)
\int_{T(\rho)}^{\infty}|r_{g}(\tau)|\mathrm{d}\tau<\delta/8,\qquad\|f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}\|A^{\rho}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}\int_{T(\rho)}^{\infty}e^{-\rho\tau}\mathrm{d}\tau<\delta/8.
Note finally that
\|P_{t}^{\rho}f-P_{t}f\|_{L^{2}}\leq(1-e^{-\rho t})\|f\|_{L^{2}}
for all f\in L^{2}(\nu) , and \|(A^{\rho}-A)f\|_{L^{2}}\leq\rho\|f\|_{L^{2}}
for all f\in D(A) . Then the statements (5.15),
(5.26),
(5.25), (5.10), (5.11),
(5.13), and (5.14)
together imply that there exists a realization of \ell_{*}:[0,T_{0}]^{2}\to\mathbb{R} depending only on \varepsilon,T_{0} and some n\geq 1 , B=B(n) , \rho>0 ,
and realization of \mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n} depending on \varepsilon,T_{0},\delta,T such that (5.27) holds for
this \rho>0 ,
(5.28) holds for the corresponding T(\rho)>0 , and
(5.29)
\displaystyle\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}|c_{g}^{0}(\tau)-\langle f_{B},P_{\tau}^{\rho}f_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}|
\displaystyle<\delta/2,
(5.30)
\displaystyle\int_{0}^{T(\rho)}|r_{g}^{\rho}(\tau)-\langle f_{B},P_{\tau}^{\rho}A^{\rho}f_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}|\mathrm{d}\tau
\displaystyle<\delta/8,
(5.31)
\displaystyle\sup_{s,t\in[0,T_{0}]}|\langle P_{t}^{\rho}f_{B},P_{s}^{\rho}A^{\rho}f_{B}\rangle-\ell_{*}(t,s)|
\displaystyle<\delta/2,
(5.32)
\displaystyle\|P_{T_{0}}^{\rho}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}
\displaystyle<\varepsilon/2,
(5.33)
\displaystyle\|f_{B}\|_{L^{2}},\|A^{\rho}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}
\displaystyle<C,
(5.34)
\displaystyle\|(P_{t}^{\rho}-P_{s}^{\rho})f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}
\displaystyle\leq C|t-s|^{1/2}+\delta/2\text{ for all }s,t\in[0,T_{0}],
(5.35)
\displaystyle\|(P_{t}^{\rho}-P_{s}^{\rho})A^{\rho}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}
\displaystyle\leq C|t-s|^{1/2}+\delta/2\text{ for all }s,t\in[0,T_{0}].
In the remainder of the proof, we fix these values of n,B,\rho
and realizations of \mathbf{X} and \ell_{*} .
Step 5 (Trotter-Kato approximation):
We now approximate {-}A^{\rho} by a finite-dimensional generator {-}A_{m} , and
apply the Trotter-Kato theorem to conclude the proof.
Since \{P_{t}^{\rho}\}_{t\geq 0} is a strongly continuous contractive semigroup,
the resolvent (\lambda\,\mathrm{Id}+A^{\rho})^{-1} of its generator
{-}A^{\rho} exists for any
\lambda>1 as a bounded linear operator (\lambda\,\mathrm{Id}+A^{\rho})^{-1}:L^{2}(\nu)\to D(A) , with inverse (\lambda\,\mathrm{Id}+A^{\rho}):D(A)\to L^{2}(\nu) [29, Theorem
1.10]. Let \{h_{i}\}_{i=1}^{\infty} be any orthonormal basis of
L^{2}(\nu) , and for each m\geq 1 , let
V_{m}=\operatorname{span}(\{(\lambda\,\mathrm{Id}+A^{\rho})^{-1}h_{i}\}_{i=1}^{m})\subset D(A).
We note that for any f\in D(A) ,
there exists f_{m}\in V_{m} for which
(5.36)
f_{m}\to f,\qquad A^{\rho}f_{m}\to A^{\rho}f\qquad\text{ in }L^{2}(\nu)\text{ as }m\to\infty.
Indeed, let
g=(\lambda\,\mathrm{Id}+A^{\rho})f , let g_{m}\in\operatorname{span}(h_{1},\ldots,h_{m}) be such that
g_{m}\to g in L^{2}(\nu) as m\to\infty ,
and let f_{m}=(\lambda\,\mathrm{Id}+A^{\rho})^{-1}g_{m} . Then, since
(\lambda\,\mathrm{Id}+A^{\rho})^{-1} is a bounded operator, f_{m}\to(\lambda\,\mathrm{Id}+A^{\rho})^{-1}g=f . Furthermore A^{\rho}f_{m}=g_{m}-\lambda f_{m} , so A^{\rho}f_{m}\to g-\lambda f=A^{\rho}f , showing
(5.36).
To define A_{m} , let \{e_{i}\}_{i=1}^{\infty} be elements
of D(A) such that \{e_{i}\}_{i=1}^{m} forms an orthonormal basis of V_{m} for
each m\geq 1 (e.g. obtained from a Gram-Schmidt procedure).
Define \Pi_{m}:L^{2}(\nu)\to\mathbb{R}^{m}
and its adjoint \Pi_{m}^{*}:\mathbb{R}^{m}\to L^{2}(\nu) (in the sense
v^{\top}\Pi_{m}f=\langle\Pi_{m}^{*}v,f\rangle_{L^{2}} ) by
\Pi_{m}f=(\langle e_{i},f\rangle_{L^{2}})_{i=1}^{m},\qquad\Pi_{m}^{*}v=\sum_{i=1}^{m}v(i)e_{i}.
Thus \Pi_{m}\Pi_{m}^{*}=\mathrm{Id} on \mathbb{R}^{m} , and
\Pi_{m}^{*}\Pi_{m}:L^{2}(\nu)\to L^{2}(\nu) is the orthogonal projector onto
V_{m} . Define A_{m}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m} by
A_{m}=\Pi_{m}A^{\rho}\Pi_{m}^{*},\qquad(A_{m})(i,j)=\langle e_{i},A^{\rho}e_{j}\rangle_{L^{2}}.
Note that for any f\in L^{2}(\nu) , we have \langle f,f-P_{t}^{\rho}f\rangle_{L^{2}}\geq(1-e^{-\rho t})\|f\|_{L^{2}}^{2}
by the contractivity \|P_{t}^{\rho}f\|_{L^{2}}=e^{-\rho t}\|P_{t}f\|_{L^{2}}\leq e^{-\rho t}\|f\|_{L^{2}}
and Cauchy-Schwarz. Hence for any f\in D(A) , we have from definition of the
generator {-}A^{\rho} that \langle f,A^{\rho}f\rangle_{L^{2}}\geq\rho\|f\|_{L^{2}}^{2} , implying
(5.37)
v^{\top}(A_{m}+A_{m}^{\top})v=2\langle\Pi_{m}^{*}v,A^{\rho}\Pi_{m}^{*}v\rangle_{L^{2}}\geq 2\rho\|v\|_{2}^{2}\text{ for all }v\in\mathbb{R}^{m}.
Thus \lambda_{\min}(A_{m}+A_{m}^{\top})\geq 2\rho , so A_{m}+A_{m}^{\top} is
strictly positive definite. This implies also, for any v\in\mathbb{R}^{m} , that
\displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\|e^{-tA_{m}}v\|_{2}^{2}
\displaystyle=-2(e^{-tA_{m}}v)^{\top}A_{m}e^{-tA_{m}}v
\displaystyle=-(e^{-tA_{m}}v)^{\top}(A_{m}+A_{m}^{\top})(e^{-tA_{m}}v)\leq-2\rho\,\|e^{-tA_{m}}v\|_{2}^{2},
so \|e^{-tA_{m}}v\|_{2}^{2}\leq e^{-2\rho t}\|v\|_{2}^{2}
and hence \|e^{-tA_{m}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq e^{-\rho t}\leq 1 for all t\geq 0 .
Thus \{P_{t}^{m}\}_{t\geq 0}:=\{e^{-tA_{m}}\}_{t\geq 0} defines
a contraction semigroup on \mathbb{R}^{m} with generator {-}A_{m} .
The property (5.36) implies that for any f\in D(A) ,
there exists u_{m}\in\mathbb{R}^{m} with \Pi_{m}^{*}u_{m}=f_{m}\in V_{m}
for each m\geq 1 such that as m\to\infty ,
(5.38)
\|\Pi_{m}^{*}u_{m}-f\|_{L^{2}}=\|f_{m}-f\|_{L^{2}}\to 0,\qquad\|A^{\rho}\Pi_{m}^{*}u_{m}-A^{\rho}f\|_{L^{2}}=\|A^{\rho}f_{m}-A^{\rho}f\|_{L^{2}}\to 0.
Hence, from the above definition A_{m}=\Pi_{m}A^{\rho}\Pi_{m}^{*} , also
\displaystyle\|\Pi_{m}^{*}A_{m}u_{m}-A^{\rho}f\|_{L^{2}}
\displaystyle=\|\Pi_{m}^{*}A_{m}\Pi_{m}f_{m}-A^{\rho}f\|_{L^{2}}=\|\Pi_{m}^{*}\Pi_{m}A^{\rho}f_{m}-A^{\rho}f\|_{L^{2}}
(5.39)
\displaystyle\leq\|\Pi_{m}^{*}\Pi_{m}A^{\rho}f-A^{\rho}f\|_{L^{2}}+\|\Pi_{m}^{*}\Pi_{m}(A^{\rho}f_{m}-A^{\rho}f)\|_{L^{2}}\to 0.
This checks property (C2) of [42, Proposition 3.1]
for D=D(A) . Property (C1) is automatic, since D(A) is dense in L^{2}(\nu)
[29, Theorem 1.4]
and (\lambda\,\mathrm{Id}+A^{\rho}):D(A)\to L^{2}(\nu) is surjective for any \lambda
in the resolvent set of {-}A^{\rho} . Thus, by the version of
the Trotter-Kato theorem stated in [42, Theorem 2.1, Proposition
3.1], for any fixed f\in L^{2}(\nu) and T>0 ,
(5.40)
\lim_{m\to\infty}\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\|\Pi_{m}^{*}P_{\tau}^{m}\Pi_{m}f-P_{\tau}^{\rho}f\|_{L^{2}}=0.
We now verify conditions (i)–(vi) of the lemma.
Recall the function f_{B} in (5.2), and let u_{m}\in\mathbb{R}^{m}
be a sequence satisfying (5.38) and (5.39)
for f=f_{B} . Let f_{m,B}\in V_{m} be such that
u_{m}=\Pi_{m}f_{m,B}\in\mathbb{R}^{m},\qquad f_{m,B}=\Pi_{m}^{*}u_{m}.
Recall that (5.29) shows
\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}|c_{g}^{0}(\tau)-\langle f_{B},P_{\tau}^{\rho}f_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}|<\delta/2 .
Applying the Trotter-Kato result (5.40) with f=f_{B} and
Cauchy-Schwarz,
(5.41)
\lim_{m\to\infty}\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}|\langle f_{B},P_{\tau}^{\rho}f_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}-\langle f_{B},\Pi_{m}^{*}P_{\tau}^{m}\Pi_{m}f_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}|=0.
Here \langle f_{B},\Pi_{m}^{*}P_{\tau}^{m}\Pi_{m}f_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}=(\Pi_{m}f_{B})^{\top}e^{-\tau A_{m}}(\Pi_{m}f_{B}) , and the first statement of
(5.38) implies
\lim_{m\to\infty}\|\Pi_{m}f_{B}-u_{m}\|_{2}=\lim_{m\to\infty}\|\Pi_{m}^{*}u_{m}-f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}=0.
Then, using \|e^{-\tau A_{m}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq 1 and Cauchy-Schwarz,
(5.42)
\lim_{m\to\infty}\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\Big|\langle f_{B},\Pi_{m}^{*}P_{\tau}^{m}\Pi_{m}f_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}-u_{m}^{\top}e^{-\tau A_{m}}u_{m}\Big|=0.
Combining (5.29),
(5.41), and (5.42) shows
statement (i) for all large enough m .
For (ii), note that
|u_{m}^{\top}A_{m}e^{-\tau A_{m}}u_{m}|\leq\|e^{-\tau A_{m}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|u_{m}\|_{2}\|A_{m}u_{m}\|_{2}\leq e^{-\tau\rho}\|u_{m}\|_{2}\|A_{m}u_{m}\|_{2}.
By (5.38) and (5.39), \|u_{m}\|_{2}\to\|f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}
and \|A_{m}u_{m}\|_{2}\to\|A^{\rho}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}} as m\to\infty . Then the second
statement of (5.28) ensures that for all large enough m ,
\int_{T(\rho)}^{\infty}|u_{m}^{\top}A_{m}e^{-\tau A_{m}}u_{m}|\mathrm{d}\tau<\delta/4.
Combining this with the first statement of
(5.28) and with (5.27) and
(5.30),
\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\infty}|r_{g}(\tau)-u_{m}^{\top}A_{m}e^{-\tau A_{m}}u_{m}|\mathrm{d}\tau
\displaystyle\leq\int_{0}^{T(\rho)}|r_{g}(\tau)-u_{m}^{\top}A_{m}e^{-\tau A_{m}}u_{m}|\mathrm{d}\tau+\int_{T(\rho)}^{\infty}|r_{g}(\tau)|\mathrm{d}\tau+\int_{T(\rho)}^{\infty}|u_{m}^{\top}A_{m}e^{-\tau A_{m}}u_{m}|\mathrm{d}\tau
(5.43)
\displaystyle\leq\int_{0}^{T(\rho)}|\langle f_{B},P_{\tau}^{\rho}A^{\rho}f_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}-u_{m}^{\top}A_{m}e^{-\tau A_{m}}u_{m}|\mathrm{d}\tau+5\delta/8.
Applying the Trotter-Kato result (5.40) with f=A^{\rho}f_{B} and
T=T(\rho) ,
\lim_{m\to\infty}\sup_{\tau\in[0,T(\rho)]}|\langle f_{B},P_{\tau}^{\rho}A^{\rho}f_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}-\langle f_{B},\Pi_{m}^{*}P_{\tau}^{m}\Pi_{m}A^{\rho}f_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}|=0.
Here \langle f_{B},\Pi_{m}^{*}P_{\tau}^{m}\Pi_{m}A^{\rho}f_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}=(\Pi_{m}f_{B})^{\top}e^{-\tau A_{m}}(\Pi_{m}A^{\rho}f_{B}) , and (5.38)
and (5.39) imply \|\Pi_{m}f_{B}-u_{m}\|_{2}\to 0
and \|\Pi_{m}A^{\rho}f_{B}-A_{m}u_{m}\|_{2}\to 0 as m\to\infty . Thus
\lim_{m\to\infty}\sup_{\tau\in[0,T(\rho)]}|\langle f_{B},P_{\tau}^{\rho}A^{\rho}f_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}-u_{m}^{\top}e^{-\tau A_{m}}A_{m}u_{m}|=0.
Applying this to (5.43) shows that (ii) holds for all
large m .
Statement (iii) follows immediately from the convergence \|u_{m}\|_{2}\to\|f_{B}\|_{L^{2}} implied by (5.38), and (5.33).
For statement (iv),
observe that at t=T_{0} ,
\displaystyle\|e^{-T_{0}A_{m}}u_{m}\|_{2}
\displaystyle=\sup_{v\in\mathbb{R}^{m}:\|v\|_{2}=1}v^{\top}e^{-T_{0}A_{m}}u_{m}
\displaystyle\leq\sup_{g\in L^{2}(\nu):\|g\|_{L^{2}}=1}(\Pi_{m}g)^{\top}e^{-T_{0}A_{m}}u_{m}=\|\Pi_{m}^{*}P_{T_{0}}^{m}u_{m}\|_{L^{2}}
\displaystyle\leq\|\Pi_{m}^{*}P_{T_{0}}^{m}\Pi_{m}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}+\|\Pi_{m}^{*}P_{T_{0}}^{m}(\Pi_{m}f_{B}-u_{m})\|_{L^{2}}
\displaystyle\leq\|\Pi_{m}^{*}P_{T_{0}}^{m}\Pi_{m}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}+\|\Pi_{m}^{*}u_{m}-f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}.
Then by the Trotter-Kato result (5.40) applied with f=f_{B} ,
T=T_{0} , and (5.38),
\limsup_{m\to\infty}\|e^{-T_{0}A_{m}}u_{m}\|_{2}\leq\lim_{m\to\infty}\|\Pi_{m}^{*}P_{T_{0}}^{m}\Pi_{m}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}+\|\Pi_{m}^{*}u_{m}-f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}=\|P_{T_{0}}^{\rho}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}.
Then (iv) holds for all large m by (5.32).
For statement (v), note similarly as above that for any s,t\geq 0 ,
\displaystyle\|(e^{-tA_{m}}-e^{-sA_{m}})u_{m}\|_{2}
\displaystyle=\|\Pi_{m}^{*}(P_{t}^{m}-P_{s}^{m})u_{m}\|_{L^{2}}
\displaystyle\leq\|\Pi_{m}^{*}(P_{t}^{m}-P_{s}^{m})\Pi_{m}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}+\|\Pi_{m}^{*}u_{m}-f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}.
Then by (5.40) applied with f=f_{B} , T=T_{0} ,
and (5.38), for any fixed \delta>0 and large enough m ,
\|(e^{-tA_{m}}-e^{-sA_{m}})u_{m}\|_{2}<\|(P_{t}^{\rho}-P_{s}^{\rho})f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}+\delta/2\text{ for all }s,t\in[0,T_{0}].
Then by (5.34),
\|(e^{-tA_{m}}-e^{-sA_{m}})u_{m}\|_{2}<C|t-s|^{1/2}+\delta . Similarly,
\displaystyle\|A_{m}(e^{-tA_{m}}-e^{-sA_{m}})u_{m}\|_{2}
\displaystyle=\|\Pi_{m}^{*}(P_{t}^{m}-P_{s}^{m})A_{m}u_{m}\|_{L^{2}}
\displaystyle\leq\|\Pi_{m}^{*}(P_{t}^{m}-P_{s}^{m})\Pi_{m}A^{\rho}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}+\|\Pi_{m}^{*}A_{m}u_{m}-A^{\rho}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}.
Applying (5.40) with f=A^{\rho}f_{B} , T=T_{0} , and
(5.39), for any \delta>0 and all large enough m ,
\|A_{m}(e^{-tA_{m}}-e^{-sA_{m}})u_{m}\|_{2}<\|(P_{t}^{\rho}-P_{s}^{\rho})A^{\rho}f_{B}\|_{L^{2}}+\delta/2\text{ for all }s,t\in[0,T_{0}].
Then by (5.35),
\|A_{m}(e^{-tA_{m}}-e^{-sA_{m}})u_{m}\|_{2}<C|t-s|^{1/2}+\delta ,
showing statement (v).
For statement (vi), note that
u_{m}^{\top}e^{-tA_{m}^{\top}}A_{m}e^{-sA_{m}}u_{m}=\langle\Pi_{m}^{*}P_{t}^{m}u_{m},\Pi_{m}^{*}P_{s}^{m}A_{m}u_{m}\rangle_{L^{2}}.
Then by the same arguments as above and Cauchy-Schwarz,
for any \delta>0 and all large enough m ,
\displaystyle\Big|u_{m}^{\top}e^{-tA_{m}^{\top}}A_{m}e^{-sA_{m}}u_{m}-\langle P_{t}^{\rho}f_{B},P_{s}^{\rho}Af_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}\Big|<\delta/2\text{ for all }s,t\in[0,T_{0}].
The bound (5.31) shows
|\langle P_{t}^{\rho}f_{B},P_{s}^{\rho}Af_{B}\rangle_{L^{2}}-\ell_{*}(t,s)|<\delta/2
for all s,t\in[0,T_{0}] , showing (vi).
∎
The above lemma implies the following coupling result for stationary
Gaussian processes with covariances c_{g}^{0}(\tau) and \tilde{c}_{g}^{m}(\tau)=u_{m}^{\top}e^{-|\tau|A_{m}}u_{m} .
Corollary 5.2.
Suppose the conditions of Theorem 2.6 hold.
Then there exists a constant C>0 such that
given any \varepsilon>0 , there exist m\geq 1 ,
u_{m}\in\mathbb{R}^{m} with \|u_{m}\|_{2}<C , and A_{m}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m} with
A_{m}+A_{m}^{\top} strictly positive definite, such that the following holds:
For all \tau\in\mathbb{R} let
c_{g}^{0}(\tau)=c_{g}(\tau)-q_{*}\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}^{\prime}(v_{*}-q_{*}),\qquad\tilde{c}_{g}^{m}(\tau)=u_{m}^{\top}e^{-|\tau|A_{m}}u_{m},
and for \tau\geq 0 let
r_{g}(\tau)=-c_{g}^{\prime}(\tau),\qquad\tilde{r}_{g}^{m}(\tau)=-(\tilde{c}_{g}^{m})^{\prime}(\tau)=u_{m}^{\top}A_{m}e^{-\tau A_{m}}u_{m}
(with derivatives understood from the right at \tau=0 ). Then
(5.44)
|\tilde{c}_{g}^{m}(0)-\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}(v_{*}-q_{*})|<\varepsilon,
(5.45)
\int_{0}^{\infty}|r_{g}(\tau)-\tilde{r}_{g}^{m}(\tau)|\,\mathrm{d}\tau<\varepsilon.
Furthermore, c_{g}^{0} and \tilde{c}_{g}^{m} are both symmetric and
positive-semidefinite on \mathbb{R} , and for any T>0 ,
there exists a coupling of two stationary Gaussian processes
\{g_{0}^{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}\sim\operatorname{GP}(0,c_{g}^{0}) and \{\tilde{g}^{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}\sim\operatorname{GP}(0,\tilde{c}_{g}^{m}) such that
(5.46)
\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\mathbb{E}(g_{0}^{t}-\tilde{g}^{t})^{2}<\varepsilon^{2}.
For our later arguments, we emphasize that the coupling (5.46) is
ensured for a single fixed m=m(\varepsilon) , and arbitrarily large T .
Proof.
Let \varepsilon be the given constant, and
let T_{0}=T_{0}(\varepsilon) be as given in Lemma 5.1. Let
\{(A_{m},u_{m})\}_{m=1}^{\infty} be a sequence of pairs in \mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\times\mathbb{R}^{m} , such that each (A_{m},u_{m}) attains the guarantees of Lemma
5.1 for (\varepsilon,T_{0}) and (\delta,T)=(\delta_{m},T_{m}) ,
where
\delta_{m}\to 0\text{ and }T_{m}\to\infty\text{ as }m\to\infty.
Recall from Lemma 4.2 that c_{g}^{0}(0)=\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}(v_{*}-q_{*}) .
Then for any m large enough such that \delta_{m}<\varepsilon , (5.44)
and (5.45)
hold by statements (i) and (ii) of Lemma 5.1.
For the coupling statement (5.46),
for each m\geq 1 , let \{b_{m}^{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}} be a standard bi-directional
Brownian motion on \mathbb{R}^{m} with b_{m}^{0}=0 ,
and let \Sigma_{m}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m} be any matrix such that
A_{m}+A_{m}^{\top}=\Sigma_{m}\Sigma_{m}^{\top} . Denote
v_{m}^{t}=\Sigma_{m}^{\top}e^{-tA_{m}}u_{m}\in\mathbb{R}^{m}.
We note that \tilde{c}_{g}^{m} is the
covariance of the Gaussian process
\tilde{g}_{m}^{t}=\int_{-\infty}^{t}v_{m}^{t-s\top}\mathrm{d}b_{m}^{s}.
Indeed, note that for any t_{0}<t ,
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left(\int_{t_{0}}^{t}v_{m}^{t-s\top}\mathrm{d}b_{m}^{s}\right)^{2}
\displaystyle=\int_{t_{0}}^{t}u_{m}^{\top}e^{-(t-s)A_{m}^{\top}}\Sigma_{m}\Sigma_{m}^{\top}e^{-(t-s)A_{m}}u_{m}\,\mathrm{d}s
\displaystyle=\int_{0}^{t-t_{0}}u_{m}^{\top}e^{-sA_{m}^{\top}}(A_{m}+A_{m}^{\top})e^{-sA_{m}}u_{m}\,\mathrm{d}s
\displaystyle=u_{m}^{\top}(I-e^{-(t-t_{0})A_{m}^{\top}}e^{-(t-t_{0})A_{m}})u_{m}
\displaystyle=\|u_{m}\|_{2}^{2}-\|e^{-(t-t_{0})A_{m}}u_{m}\|_{2}^{2}\leq\|u_{m}\|_{2}^{2}.
Since A_{m}+A_{m}^{\top} is positive definite, we have
\|e^{-tA_{m}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}<1 and
\|e^{-(t-t_{0})A_{m}}u_{m}\|_{2}^{2}\to 0 as t_{0}\to-\infty . Then \tilde{g}_{m}^{t} is
well-defined, and \mathbb{E}(\tilde{g}_{m}^{t})^{2}=\|u_{m}\|_{2}^{2}=\tilde{c}_{g}^{m}(0) .
An analogous calculation shows, for s\leq t ,
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\tilde{g}_{m}^{s}\tilde{g}_{m}^{t}
\displaystyle=u_{m}^{\top}\left(\int_{-\infty}^{s}e^{-(s-r)A_{m}^{\top}}(A_{m}+A_{m}^{\top})e^{-(s-r)A_{m}}\mathrm{d}r\right)e^{-(t-s)A_{m}}u_{m}
\displaystyle=u_{m}^{\top}e^{-(t-s)A_{m}}u_{m}=\tilde{c}_{g}^{m}(t-s),
so \tilde{c}_{g}^{m}(\tau) is the covariance of \{\tilde{g}_{m}^{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}} as
claimed. In particular, \tilde{c}_{g}^{m} is symmetric positive-semidefinite.
Let us first couple \{\tilde{g}_{m}^{t}\}\sim\operatorname{GP}(0,\tilde{c}_{g}^{m}) and
\{\tilde{g}_{n}^{t}\}\sim\operatorname{GP}(0,\tilde{c}_{g}^{n}) :
Property (iv) of Lemma 5.1 ensures
\int_{T_{0}}^{\infty}\|v_{m}^{t}\|_{2}^{2}\mathrm{d}t=\int_{T_{0}}^{\infty}u_{m}^{\top}e^{-tA_{m}^{\top}}(A_{m}+A_{m}^{\top})e^{-tA_{m}}u_{m}\mathrm{d}t=\|e^{-T_{0}A_{m}}u_{m}\|_{2}^{2}<\varepsilon^{2}
for all m\geq 1 . Set \gamma=\varepsilon^{2}/T_{0} .
For any t\in[0,T_{0}] , let
\lfloor t\rfloor=\max\{k\gamma:k\in\mathbb{N},k\gamma\leq t\} be the largest
integer multiple of \gamma that is at most t . Then by property (v) of Lemma
5.1, for all m\geq 1 for which \delta_{m}<\gamma^{1/2}
and T_{m}>T_{0} , we have
\displaystyle\int_{0}^{T_{0}}\|v_{m}^{t}-v_{m}^{\lfloor t\rfloor}\|_{2}^{2}\mathrm{d}t
\displaystyle=\int_{0}^{T_{0}}2u_{m}^{\top}(e^{-tA_{m}^{\top}}-e^{-\lfloor t\rfloor A_{m}^{\top}})A_{m}(e^{-tA_{m}}-e^{-\lfloor t\rfloor A_{m}})u_{m}\mathrm{d}t
\displaystyle<CT_{0}\gamma=C\varepsilon^{2}.
Let E=[0,T_{0}]\cap\{k\gamma:k\in\mathbb{N}\} . Then property
(vi) of Lemma 5.1 ensures that
\displaystyle\lim_{m,n\to\infty}\sup_{s,t\in E}|v_{m}^{s\top}v_{m}^{t}-v_{n}^{s\top}v_{n}^{t}|
\displaystyle=\lim_{m,n\to\infty}\sup_{s,t\in E}|2u_{m}^{\top}e^{-sA_{m}^{\top}}A_{m}e^{-tA_{m}}u_{m}-2u_{n}^{\top}e^{-sA_{n}^{\top}}A_{n}e^{-tA_{n}}u_{n}|=0.
Then we may construct, for each pair m,n\geq 1 , some
N=N(n,m) and isometric embeddings \iota_{m}:\mathbb{R}^{m}\to\mathbb{R}^{N} and
\iota_{n}:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}^{N} , such that
\lim_{m,n\to\infty}\sup_{t\in E}\|\iota_{m}(v_{m}^{t})-\iota_{n}(v_{n}^{t})\|_{2}=0.
(For example, letting K_{m}\in\mathbb{R}^{|E|\times|E|} and K_{n}\in\mathbb{R}^{|E|\times|E|} have entries (v_{m}^{s\top}v_{m}^{t})_{s,t\in E}
and (v_{n}^{s\top}v_{n}^{t})_{s,t\in E} , we may set N(n,m)=|E| ,
\iota_{m}(v_{m}^{t})=K_{m}^{1/2}e_{t} , and \iota_{n}(v_{n}^{t})=K_{n}^{1/2}e_{t}
where e_{t} is the standard basis vector in \mathbb{R}^{|E|} for each t\in E .)
Then, letting \{b_{N}^{t}\}_{t\geq 0} be a standard Brownian motion on \mathbb{R}^{N} ,
we may couple \{\tilde{g}_{m}^{t}\}\sim\operatorname{GP}(0,\tilde{c}_{g}^{m}) and
\{\tilde{g}_{n}^{t}\}\sim\operatorname{GP}(0,\tilde{c}_{g}^{n}) as
\tilde{g}_{m}^{t}=\int_{-\infty}^{t}\iota_{m}(v_{m}^{t-s})^{\top}\mathrm{d}b_{N}^{s},\qquad\tilde{g}_{n}^{t}=\int_{-\infty}^{t}\iota_{n}(v_{n}^{t-s})^{\top}\mathrm{d}b_{N}^{s}.
Denoting by \mathbb{E}_{\pi(m,n)} the expectation over this coupling,
for any m,n\geq 1 such that
\delta_{m},\delta_{n}<\iota^{1/2} and T_{m},T_{n}>T_{0} , we then have
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\pi(m,n)}(\tilde{g}_{m}^{t}-\tilde{g}_{n}^{t})^{2}
\displaystyle=\int_{-\infty}^{t}\|\iota_{m}(v_{m}^{t-s})-\iota_{n}(v_{n}^{t-s})\|_{2}^{2}\mathrm{d}s=\int_{0}^{\infty}\|\iota_{m}(v_{m}^{s})-\iota_{n}(v_{n}^{s})\|_{2}^{2}\mathrm{d}s
\displaystyle\leq 3\int_{0}^{T_{0}}\left(\|v_{m}^{s}-v_{m}^{\lfloor s\rfloor}\|_{2}^{2}+\|v_{n}^{s}-v_{n}^{\lfloor s\rfloor}\|_{2}^{2}+\|\iota_{m}(v_{m}^{\lfloor s\rfloor})-\iota_{n}(v_{n}^{\lfloor s\rfloor})\|_{2}^{2}\right)\mathrm{d}s
\displaystyle\hskip 72.26999pt+2\int_{T_{0}}^{\infty}\left(\|v_{m}^{s}\|_{2}^{2}+\|v_{n}^{s}\|_{2}^{2}\right)\mathrm{d}s
\displaystyle\leq C^{\prime}\varepsilon^{2}+3\int_{0}^{T_{0}}\|\iota_{m}(v_{m}^{\lfloor s\rfloor})-\iota_{n}(v_{n}^{\lfloor s\rfloor})\|_{2}^{2}\mathrm{d}s
for a constant C>0 . Thus
\lim_{m,n\to\infty}\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{E}_{\pi(m,n)}(\tilde{g}_{m}^{t}-\tilde{g}_{n}^{t})^{2}\leq C^{\prime}\varepsilon^{2},
implying that there exists a fixed index m=m(\varepsilon) large enough so that
\delta_{m}<\iota^{1/2} , T_{m}>T_{0} , and
