the joint law of \{(\theta^{t},g^{t},b^{t})\}_{t\geq 0} in the dynamical
mean-field limit of Definition 2.3 is also invariant under
multiplication by a single sign s\in\{\pm 1\} . Setting
\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}=\mathbf{S}\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\top}\boldsymbol{\theta}^{t},\qquad\tilde{\mathbf{g}}^{t}=\mathbf{S}\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\top}\mathbf{g}^{t},\qquad\tilde{\mathbf{b}}^{t}=\mathbf{S}\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\top}\mathbf{b}^{t},
the conclusion of Theorem 2.4
for \{(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{t},\mathbf{g}^{t},\mathbf{b}^{t})\}_{t\geq 0} implies that the empirical
distribution of sample paths of
\{(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t},\tilde{\mathbf{g}}^{t},\tilde{\mathbf{b}}^{t})\}_{t\geq 0} converges to
the law of \{(s\theta^{t},sg^{t},sb^{t})\}_{t\geq 0} where s\in\{\pm 1\} is
an independent and uniformly random sign. This is the same law as
that of \{(\theta^{t},g^{t},b^{t})\}_{t\geq 0} , so Theorem 2.4
holds also for \{(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t},\tilde{\mathbf{g}}^{t},\tilde{\mathbf{b}}^{t})\}_{t\geq 0} .
Since \mathbf{S}\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\top}f(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{t})=f(\mathbf{S}\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\top}\boldsymbol{\theta}^{t})=f(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}) when
f(\cdot) is odd, we have
\mathrm{d}\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}=[f(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t})+\tilde{\mathbf{X}}\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}]\mathrm{d}t+\sqrt{2\gamma}\,\mathrm{d}\tilde{\mathbf{b}}^{t},\qquad\tilde{\mathbf{g}}^{t}=\tilde{\mathbf{X}}\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{t}-\int_{0}^{t}r_{g}(t-s)\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{s}\mathrm{d}s
coinciding with the dynamics (2.1) driven by \tilde{\mathbf{X}} .
This shows
Corollary 2.10(a). If U(\cdot) is even and h=0 in the
Ising model, then the Gibbs measures \mu_{\mathrm{Gibbs}} and \mu_{\text{Ising}} defined
by \mathbf{W} are also identical to those defined by \tilde{\mathbf{X}} , implying
Corollary 2.10(b–c).
∎
Appendix A Free cumulant bound
Proposition A.1.
Suppose \Lambda is a random variable with |\Lambda|\leq K
for a constant K>0 . Let \{\kappa_{p}\}_{p\geq 1} be the free
cumulants of \Lambda . Then
\limsup_{p\to\infty}|\kappa_{p}|^{1/p}\leq 2K.
Proof.
By rescaling \Lambda , assume without loss of generality K=1 .
For z\in\mathbb{C} outside the support of \Lambda , define the Cauchy transform
\mathcal{G}_{\Lambda}(z)=\mathbb{E}[1/(z-\Lambda)] . It is shown in [53, Theorem
17] that \mathcal{G}_{\Lambda} is univalent over \{z:|z|>4\} , that
\{w:|w|\in(0,1/6)\}\subset\mathcal{G}_{\Lambda}(\{z:|z|>4\}) , and that
\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}(w) defined by (2.13) is absolutely
convergent for |w|<1/6 and given by
(A.1)
\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}(w)=\mathcal{G}_{\Lambda}^{-1}(w)-\frac{1}{w}\text{ for }|w|\in(0,1/6)
where \mathcal{G}_{\Lambda}^{-1}(w) denotes the unique inverse in \{z:|z|>4\} .
We check that \mathcal{R}_{\Lambda} extends analytically to |w|<1/2 :
Define, on the open disk
\mathbb{D}=\{z:|z|<1\} , the analytic function
H(z)=\mathcal{G}_{\Lambda}(1/z)=\mathbb{E}[z/(1-z\Lambda)].
For any z\in\mathbb{D} and |\Lambda|\leq 1 , note that
|1-z\Lambda|^{2}\leq 1+\Lambda^{2}-2\Re[z]\Lambda\leq(2+\varepsilon)(1-\Re[z]\Lambda) .
Then \Re[1/(1-z\Lambda)]=(1-\Re[z]\Lambda)/|1-z\Lambda|^{2}\geq 1/(2+\varepsilon) .
This implies \mathbb{E}[1/(1-z\Lambda)]\neq 0 ,
so z=0 is the unique simple root of H(z) on \mathbb{D} . Furthermore,
|H(z)|\geq|z|\cdot\Re\,\mathbb{E}[1/(1-z\Lambda)]\geq\frac{1-\varepsilon}{2+\varepsilon}\text{ for }|z|=1-\varepsilon.
Then by Rouché’s theorem, for each w\in\mathbb{C} with |w|<(1-\varepsilon)/(2+\varepsilon) ,
H(z)=w also has a unique simple root z in the disk \{z:|z|<1-\varepsilon\} .
Since H^{\prime}(z)\neq 0 at this root,
the inverse function theorem implies that there exists an analytic
inverse H^{-1} on \{w:|w|<(1-\varepsilon)/(2+\varepsilon)\} .
Since H^{-1}(0)=0 , we have |H^{-1}(w)|<1/4 on some neighborhood \mathcal{O}
of w=0 , and \mathcal{G}_{\Lambda}(1/H^{-1}(w))=H(H^{-1}(w))=w . Then the
above univalence implies 1/H^{-1}(w)=\mathcal{G}_{\Lambda}^{-1}(w) for all w\in\mathcal{O} .
Then the right side of (A.1) has an analytic extension
to \{w:|w|\in(0,(1-\varepsilon)/(2+\varepsilon))\} . Since \varepsilon>0 is arbitrary, this
implies \mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}(w) extends analytically to |w|<1/2 , as claimed. Then
\mathcal{R}_{\Lambda}(w) is given by the convergent series (2.13)
for all |w|<1/2 , so the root test implies that \limsup_{p\to\infty}|\kappa_{p}|^{1/p}\leq 2 .
∎

Z.F. would like to thank Rishabh Dudeja for helpful conversations about the dynamical approach to free energy universality. This research was supported in part by NSF DMS-2142476 and a Sloan Research Fellowship.
Statement on AI use
Several supporting proof ideas were obtained in dialogue with ChatGPT (GPT-5.5) over the course of this research: the Gaussian coupling construction of Corollary 5.2, the Gaussian mixture interpolation of Corollary 2.8, the extension from Hölder-continuity to continuous-differentiability concluding the proof of Theorem
2.6(b), and the free cumulant bound of Proposition A.1. The authors assume responsibility for the correctness of all stated results.

Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
all.
Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a list of packages that need conversion, and welcome developer contributions.
